solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ape))

# 1. Load input data
# Reads aligned DNA sequences from FASTA file
message("1. Loading woodmouse sequences (FASTA)...")
fasta_file <- file.path("inputs", "woodmouse.fasta")
if (!file.exists(fasta_file)) {
    stop("Input file 'inputs/woodmouse.fasta' not found.")
}

# read.dna reads sequences into a DNAbin object
# format="fasta" implies we are reading a standard alignment
woodmouse_dna <- read.dna(fasta_file, format = "fasta")

# 2. Compute Distance Matrix (Kimura 80 Model)
# We use the Kimura 2-parameter model (K80) which accounts for transitions vs transversions
# 'pairwise.deletion = TRUE' handles gaps by ignoring sites with gaps in pairwise comparisons
message("2. Computing genetic distances (K80)...")
dist_mat <- dist.dna(woodmouse_dna, model = "K80", pairwise.deletion = TRUE)

# 3. Build Phylogenetic Tree (Neighbor-Joining)
# Neighbor-Joining is a fast, distance-based method for tree construction
message("3. Constructing Neighbor-Joining tree...")
nj_tree <- nj(dist_mat)

# 4. Save outputs
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save distance matrix as CSV
# Convert dist object to matrix then dataframe
dist_df <- as.matrix(dist_mat)
write.csv(dist_df, file = file.path(output_dir, "genetic_distances.csv"))

# Save the tree in Newick format (standard for phylogenetics)
write.tree(nj_tree, file = file.path(output_dir, "nj_tree.nwk"))

# Save tree statistics
tree_stats <- data.frame(
    num_tips = length(nj_tree$tip.label),
    num_nodes = nj_tree$Nnode,
    total_branch_length = sum(nj_tree$edge.length)
)
write.csv(tree_stats, file = file.path(output_dir, "tree_stats.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

message("Analysis complete. Results saved to outputs/")

prompt: Write R code to construct a well-annotated ExpressionSet from RNA-seq count data using Biobase. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(Biobase). The raw gene-by-sample count matrix is stored in inputs/counts.tsv and the associated clinical metadata, including sample-level information such as group assignment, is in inputs/clinical.tsv, and you should carefully align the count matrix columns with the clinical rows so that sample identifiers match. Use Biobase’s ExpressionSet function together with AnnotatedDataFrame objects for both phenoData (built from the clinical table) and featureData (built from the genes, including a per-gene mean_expression column computed from the counts), ensuring that the counts populate the assayData, and rely only on Biobase and its documented helpers for all of this construction. After creating the ExpressionSet, save it as an RDS file at outputs/expression_set.rds and also generate a per-sample CSV summary at outputs/expression_summary.csv that records, for each sample, the total_counts, the number of detected_genes, and its group. Before finishing, confirm that both the RDS and CSV files were written, quickly review a few rows of the summary for plausible library sizes and detected gene counts, and check for unexpected NA-heavy or zero-inflated patterns that might indicate misalignment or parsing issues.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Biobase))

counts_path <- file.path("inputs", "counts.tsv")
clinical_path <- file.path("inputs", "clinical.tsv")
if (!file.exists(counts_path) || !file.exists(clinical_path)) {
  stop("counts.tsv and clinical.tsv are required inputs")
}

expr_df <- read.delim(counts_path, check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
expr_mat <- as.matrix(expr_df)

clinical_df <- read.delim(clinical_path, check.names = FALSE)
if (!"sample" %in% colnames(clinical_df)) {
  stop("clinical.tsv must contain a 'sample' column")
}

common_samples <- intersect(colnames(expr_mat), clinical_df$sample)
if (length(common_samples) == 0) {
  stop("No overlapping samples between counts and clinical metadata")
}
expr_mat <- expr_mat[, common_samples, drop = FALSE]
clinical_df <- clinical_df[match(common_samples, clinical_df$sample), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(clinical_df) <- clinical_df$sample

feature_df <- data.frame(
  gene_id = rownames(expr_mat),
  mean_expression = rowMeans(expr_mat),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  row.names = rownames(expr_mat)
)

pheno_data <- AnnotatedDataFrame(clinical_df)
feature_data <- AnnotatedDataFrame(feature_df)

eset <- ExpressionSet(assayData = expr_mat, phenoData = pheno_data, featureData = feature_data)

exprs_mat <- exprs(eset)
sample_summary <- data.frame(
  sample = colnames(exprs_mat),
  total_counts = colSums(exprs_mat),
  detected_genes = colSums(exprs_mat > 0),
  group = pData(eset)$group,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(eset, file.path(outputs_dir, "expression_set.rds"))
write.csv(sample_summary, file.path(outputs_dir, "expression_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

prompt: Write R code to build a log-transformed ExpressionSet from RNA-seq count and clinical data using Biobase. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(Biobase). Starting from the raw count matrix in inputs/counts.tsv and the clinical annotations in inputs/clinical.tsv, align samples between the two tables, apply a log2(count + 1) transformation to the counts, and construct a Biobase::ExpressionSet in which the clinical metadata rows correctly match the expression columns. Use Biobase utilities, including Biobase::write.exprs, to export the normalized expression matrix as a tab-separated file at outputs/log_counts.tsv, save the complete ExpressionSet object to outputs/log_expression_set.rds with saveRDS, and create a QC summary data frame with one row per sample (including sample, mean_expression derived from the log-transformed matrix, and status from the clinical data) that you write to outputs/eset_qc.csv. Please rely only on Biobase and its standard helpers rather than adding other expression analysis packages, and as a basic quality check confirm that all three output files are created, inspect a few rows to verify sample alignment and expression ranges, and check for any NA-heavy samples or obvious outliers in the mean_expression values.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Biobase))

counts_path <- file.path("inputs", "counts.tsv")
clinical_path <- file.path("inputs", "clinical.tsv")
if (!file.exists(counts_path) || !file.exists(clinical_path)) {
  stop("counts.tsv and clinical.tsv must exist")
}

counts_df <- read.delim(counts_path, check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
clinical_df <- read.delim(clinical_path, check.names = FALSE)
if (!"sample" %in% names(clinical_df)) {
  stop("clinical metadata must include a 'sample' column")
}

common <- intersect(colnames(counts_df), clinical_df$sample)
if (length(common) == 0) {
  stop("Found no overlapping samples between counts and clinical data")
}
counts_df <- counts_df[, common, drop = FALSE]
clinical_df <- clinical_df[match(common, clinical_df$sample), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(clinical_df) <- clinical_df$sample

log_counts <- log2(counts_df + 1)
exprs_mat <- as.matrix(log_counts)

feature_df <- data.frame(
  gene_id = rownames(exprs_mat),
  detected = rowSums(exprs_mat > 0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  row.names = rownames(exprs_mat)
)

eset <- ExpressionSet(
  assayData = exprs_mat,
  phenoData = AnnotatedDataFrame(clinical_df),
  featureData = AnnotatedDataFrame(feature_df)
)

outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.exprs(eset, file = file.path(outputs_dir, "log_counts.tsv"), sep = "\t", col.names = NA)
saveRDS(eset, file.path(outputs_dir, "log_expression_set.rds"))

qc_df <- data.frame(
  sample = sampleNames(eset),
  mean_expression = colMeans(exprs(eset)),
  status = pData(eset)$status,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
write.csv(qc_df, file.path(outputs_dir, "eset_qc.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

prompt: Write R code to construct a curated clinical phenotype object as a Biobase AnnotatedDataFrame using Biobase. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(Biobase). This phenotype object will provide well-annotated sample-level clinical data for downstream analyses such as survival modeling and group-wise comparisons, so start by reading the clinical table from inputs/clinical.tsv, coercing the group column to a factor and both status and time columns to numeric, and setting the row names to match the sample column. Use the AnnotatedDataFrame function to wrap this clinical data frame, and populate the varMetadata slot with clear labelDescription entries for each column so that the meaning of group, status, time, and any derived fields is explicit. In the same script, summarize the cohort by group, computing for each group the number of samples and the mean survival time, and write this summary table to outputs/clinical_summary.csv while saving the AnnotatedDataFrame object itself as outputs/annotated_pheno.rds, relying only on Biobase (plus base R) rather than bringing in other annotation or IO-focused packages. As a quick quality check, confirm that both output files are created, inspect the per-group counts and mean survival times for biological plausibility, and look for unexpected NA values or impossible survival durations.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Biobase))

clinical_path <- file.path("inputs", "clinical.tsv")
if (!file.exists(clinical_path)) {
  stop("clinical.tsv not found")
}

clinical_df <- read.delim(clinical_path, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
required_cols <- c("sample", "group", "status", "time")
missing <- setdiff(required_cols, names(clinical_df))
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  stop("clinical.tsv missing required columns: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}

clinical_df$group <- factor(clinical_df$group)
clinical_df$status <- as.numeric(clinical_df$status)
clinical_df$time <- as.numeric(clinical_df$time)
row.names(clinical_df) <- clinical_df$sample

clinical_df$sample_id <- clinical_df$sample
clinical_df$survival_time <- clinical_df$time

col_desc <- c(
  sample = "Sample identifier",
  group = "Group assignment",
  status = "Event indicator",
  time = "Follow-up time (days)",
  sample_id = "Alias for sample",
  survival_time = "Alias for time"
)
var_md <- data.frame(
  labelDescription = col_desc[colnames(clinical_df)],
  row.names = colnames(clinical_df)
)

annot_pheno <- AnnotatedDataFrame(data = clinical_df, varMetadata = var_md)

summary_df <- aggregate(
  list(n_samples = clinical_df$sample),
  by = list(group = clinical_df$group),
  FUN = length
)
summary_time <- aggregate(
  list(mean_time = clinical_df$time),
  by = list(group = clinical_df$group),
  FUN = mean
)
summary_df <- merge(summary_df, summary_time, by = "group", all = TRUE)

outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(annot_pheno, file.path(outputs_dir, "annotated_pheno.rds"))
write.csv(summary_df, file.path(outputs_dir, "clinical_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

prompt: Write R code to filter an ExpressionSet to treatment samples and highly expressed genes using Biobase. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(Biobase). Starting from the expression matrix in inputs/counts.tsv and the sample annotations in inputs/clinical.tsv, construct an ExpressionSet with appropriate phenotype and feature data, then use the Biobase subset function together with standard accessors like exprs and pData to first retain only samples whose group field equals “Treatment” in a case-insensitive way and then restrict to genes whose mean expression across these samples is greater than 50. Use Biobase where convenient; output-equivalent implementations are acceptable for building the ExpressionSet, performing the subsetting, and calculating the necessary summaries, and save the resulting filtered ExpressionSet object as an RDS file at outputs/filtered_eset.rds along with a CSV summary table at outputs/filter_summary.csv containing total_genes, kept_genes, total_samples, kept_samples, and mean_expression_kept. As a basic quality check, confirm that both output files are created, review the summary values to ensure that some samples and genes are actually retained, and quickly scan the filtered expression values for unexpected NAs or extreme outliers.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Biobase))

counts_path <- file.path("inputs", "counts.tsv")
clinical_path <- file.path("inputs", "clinical.tsv")
if (!file.exists(counts_path) || !file.exists(clinical_path)) {
  stop("counts.tsv and clinical.tsv are required")
}
counts_df <- read.delim(counts_path, check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
expr_mat <- as.matrix(counts_df)
clinical_df <- read.delim(clinical_path, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
if (!"sample" %in% names(clinical_df)) stop("clinical.tsv must contain 'sample'")
common <- intersect(colnames(expr_mat), clinical_df$sample)
if (length(common) == 0) stop("No overlapping samples between counts and clinical data")
expr_mat <- expr_mat[, common, drop = FALSE]
clinical_df <- clinical_df[match(common, clinical_df$sample), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(clinical_df) <- clinical_df$sample

feature_df <- data.frame(gene_id = rownames(expr_mat), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = rownames(expr_mat))
eset <- ExpressionSet(expr_mat, AnnotatedDataFrame(clinical_df), AnnotatedDataFrame(feature_df))

sel_samples <- grepl("^treatment$", pData(eset)$group, ignore.case = TRUE)
eset_filtered <- eset[, sel_samples, drop = FALSE]
mean_expr <- rowMeans(exprs(eset_filtered))
sel_genes <- mean_expr > 50
eset_filtered <- eset_filtered[sel_genes, , drop = FALSE]

filtered_expr <- exprs(eset_filtered)
summary_df <- data.frame(
  total_genes = nrow(exprs(eset)),
  kept_genes = nrow(filtered_expr),
  total_samples = ncol(exprs(eset)),
  kept_samples = ncol(filtered_expr),
  mean_expression_kept = if (nrow(filtered_expr) > 0) mean(filtered_expr) else 0
)

outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(eset_filtered, file.path(outputs_dir, "filtered_eset.rds"))
write.csv(summary_df, file.path(outputs_dir, "filter_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

prompt: Write R code to construct an ExpressionSet and quantify group-wise gene expression variability using Biobase. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(Biobase). The goal is to take the raw count matrix in inputs/counts.tsv together with the clinical annotation in inputs/clinical.tsv, align samples between these two tables by their shared sample identifiers, and then use the ExpressionSet constructor (with appropriate phenoData from the clinical table and featureData keyed by gene IDs) to create a coherent ExpressionSet object. Within this Biobase framework, and without bringing in any additional toolkits, compute per-gene mean expression, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation separately for each clinical group defined by the “group” column, then write a tidy variability report to outputs/group_variability_report.csv with columns gene, group, mean_expression, sd_expression, and cv, and a simple group-level sample count summary to outputs/group_sample_summary.csv, and save the finalized ExpressionSet as outputs/group_variability_eset.rds. This analysis will help you understand how stable or heterogeneous each gene’s expression is within different clinical groups, which can highlight potential biomarkers or group-specific regulatory patterns. As basic QC, verify that all three output files are created, skim a few rows of the variability and sample summary tables for plausible ranges and group labels, and check for excessive NA values or zero-variance patterns that might signal misalignment or parsing problems.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Biobase))

counts_path <- file.path("inputs", "counts.tsv")
clinical_path <- file.path("inputs", "clinical.tsv")
if (!file.exists(counts_path)) stop("counts.tsv missing")
if (!file.exists(clinical_path)) stop("clinical.tsv missing")

counts_df <- read.delim(counts_path, check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
clinical_df <- read.delim(clinical_path, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
if (!"sample" %in% colnames(clinical_df)) stop("clinical.tsv missing 'sample' column")
if (!"group" %in% colnames(clinical_df)) stop("clinical.tsv missing 'group' column")

sample_overlap <- intersect(colnames(counts_df), clinical_df$sample)
if (length(sample_overlap) == 0) stop("No overlapping samples between counts and clinical metadata")
counts_aligned <- counts_df[, sample_overlap, drop = FALSE]
clinical_aligned <- clinical_df[match(sample_overlap, clinical_df$sample), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(clinical_aligned) <- clinical_aligned$sample
expr_mat <- as.matrix(counts_aligned)

feature_df <- data.frame(gene = rownames(expr_mat), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = rownames(expr_mat))
pheno <- AnnotatedDataFrame(clinical_aligned)
feature <- AnnotatedDataFrame(feature_df)
eset <- ExpressionSet(assayData = expr_mat, phenoData = pheno, featureData = feature)

if (!"group" %in% varLabels(eset)) stop("group column missing in phenoData")
groups <- unique(as.character(pData(eset)$group))
report_list <- vector("list", length(groups))

for (i in seq_along(groups)) {
  g <- groups[[i]]
  idx <- which(pData(eset)$group == g)
  if (length(idx) == 0) next
  mat_subset <- exprs(eset)[, idx, drop = FALSE]
  means <- rowMeans(mat_subset)
  sds <- if (ncol(mat_subset) == 1) rep(0, nrow(mat_subset)) else apply(mat_subset, 1, sd)
  cv <- ifelse(means == 0, NA_real_, sds / means)
  report_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
    gene = rownames(mat_subset),
    group = g,
    mean_expression = means,
    sd_expression = sds,
    cv = cv,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
report_list <- report_list[!vapply(report_list, is.null, logical(1))]
report_df <- if (length(report_list) > 0) do.call(rbind, report_list) else data.frame(
  gene = character(0),
  group = character(0),
  mean_expression = numeric(0),
  sd_expression = numeric(0),
  cv = numeric(0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

summary_df <- aggregate(sample ~ group, data = clinical_aligned, FUN = length)
names(summary_df) <- c("group", "sample_count")

outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(report_df, file.path(outputs_dir, "group_variability_report.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(summary_df, file.path(outputs_dir, "group_sample_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(eset, file.path(outputs_dir, "group_variability_eset.rds"))

solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
library(BiocGenerics)
counts <- as.matrix(read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))

thresh <- quantile(row_means, 0.75)
filtered <- Filter(function(idx) row_means[idx] >= thresh, as.list(seq_len(nrow(counts))))
result <- data.frame(gene = rownames(counts)[unlist(filtered)], mean_expr = row_means[unlist(filtered)])
if (!dir.exists('outputs')) dir.create('outputs', recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(result, 'outputs/high_expression_genes.csv', row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(threshold = thresh, kept = nrow(result)), 'outputs/filter_summary.csv', row.names = FALSE)

solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

prompt: Write R code to compute per-sample column sums from a gene expression count matrix using BiocParallel. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(BiocParallel). The input counts matrix is stored as a tab-delimited file at inputs/counts.tsv, where each column is a sample and each row is a gene, and the resulting column-wise sums will give a quick view of total sequencing depth or library size per sample, which is useful for early QC and normalization decisions in RNA-seq or similar workflows. Read this matrix into R, split the sample columns into sensible chunks, and use BiocParallel::bplapply with a SerialParam backend to compute column sums for each chunk, then combine the partial results into a single data frame and write it as a CSV file to outputs/column_sums.csv; in parallel, create a small parameter summary (for example the number of workers, the backend class, and the total number of samples) and save it as outputs/param_summary.csv in CSV format. Make sure you rely only on BiocParallel and its documented helpers, particularly bplapply and SerialParam, and do not introduce other parallel or apply frameworks. As a final quality check, confirm that both CSV files are created, quickly review the summed counts for unexpected zeros, extreme outliers, or NA-heavy columns, and ensure the parameter summary matches the configuration you intended to use.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
library(BiocParallel)

counts <- as.matrix(read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))

# Split columns into roughly equal chunks for parallel processing
n_chunks <- min(4, ncol(counts))
chunk_index <- split(seq_len(ncol(counts)), rep(1:n_chunks, length.out = ncol(counts)))

param <- SerialParam(progressbar = FALSE)
partial <- bplapply(chunk_index, function(idx) {
  data.frame(sample = colnames(counts)[idx], sum = colSums(counts[, idx, drop = FALSE]))
}, BPPARAM = param)

solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Biostrings))

# 1. Load sequence
message("1. Loading sequence from FASTA...")
fasta_file <- file.path("inputs", "dm3_upstream.fasta")
if (!file.exists(fasta_file)) stop("Input file missing.")
# readDNAStringSet returns a DNAStringSet object
dna_seqs <- readDNAStringSet(fasta_file)
# We assume a single genome record
genome <- dna_seqs[[1]]

# 2. Basic Statistics
# Calculate nucleotide frequencies
message("2. Calculating nucleotide frequencies...")
nuc_counts <- alphabetFrequency(genome, baseOnly = TRUE)
nuc_df <- data.frame(Base = names(nuc_counts), Count = as.integer(nuc_counts))
# Add GC content
gc_count <- sum(nuc_counts[c("G", "C")])
total_bases <- sum(nuc_counts)
gc_content <- gc_count / total_bases

# 3. K-mer Analysis (Dinucleotides)
message("3. Calculating dinucleotide frequencies...")
dinuc_counts <- dinucleotideFrequency(genome)
dinuc_df <- data.frame(Dinucleotide = names(dinuc_counts), Count = as.integer(dinuc_counts))
dinuc_df <- dinuc_df[order(-dinuc_df$Count), ]

# 4. Motif Search (Restriction Sites)
# EcoRI: GAATTC
# BamHI: GGATCC
# HindIII: AAGCTT
message("4. Searching for restriction sites...")
motifs <- c("EcoRI" = "GAATTC", "BamHI" = "GGATCC", "HindIII" = "AAGCTT")

all_hits <- data.frame()

for (enzyme in names(motifs)) {
    pattern <- motifs[[enzyme]]
    # Match pattern in the genome
    hits <- matchPattern(pattern, genome)
    
    if (length(hits) > 0) {
        # Extract coordinates
        hit_df <- data.frame(
            Enzyme = enzyme,
            Pattern = pattern,
            Start = start(hits),
            End = end(hits),
            Strand = "+" # matchPattern searches the subject string (forward strand)
        )
        all_hits <- rbind(all_hits, hit_df)
    }
    
    # Also search reverse complement?
    # Restriction sites are often palindromic, so searching + strand finds the site.
    # e.g. GAATTC reverse complement is GAATTC.
    # So searching the forward strand is sufficient for palindromic sites.
}

# 5. Open Reading Frame (ORF) Finding (Naive)
# Find all ATG start codons
message("5. Finding naive Open Reading Frames (ORFs)...")
starts <- matchPattern("ATG", genome)
# For a quick demonstration, we just report ATG locations, as full ORF finding is complex
# (requires finding in-frame stop codons).
# Let's save the first 100 potential start sites
orf_starts <- data.frame(
    Start_Codon = "ATG",
    Position = start(starts)
)
if (nrow(orf_starts) > 100) orf_starts <- head(orf_starts, 100)

# 6. Save outputs
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save Statistics
stats_list <- list(
    GC_Content = gc_content,
    Total_Length = length(genome)
)
# Write stats to a simple CSV
write.csv(data.frame(Metric = names(stats_list), Value = unlist(stats_list)), 
          file = file.path(output_dir, "sequence_stats.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save Nucleotide Counts
write.csv(nuc_df, file = file.path(output_dir, "nucleotide_counts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save Dinucleotide Counts
write.csv(dinuc_df, file = file.path(output_dir, "dinucleotide_counts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save Motif Hits
if (nrow(all_hits) > 0) {
    write.csv(all_hits, file = file.path(output_dir, "restriction_sites.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
    message("No restriction sites found.")
    # Create empty file structure
    write.csv(data.frame(Enzyme=character(), Pattern=character(), Start=integer(), End=integer(), Strand=character()),
              file = file.path(output_dir, "restriction_sites.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

# Save ORF starts
write.csv(orf_starts, file = file.path(output_dir, "orf_starts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

message("Analysis complete. Results saved to outputs/")

prompt: Perform ChIP-seq peak annotation using the 'ChIPseeker' package. Load the ChIP-seq peak file from 'inputs/sample_peaks.bed.gz' using 'readPeakFile'. Annotate the peaks with genomic features using 'annotatePeak' with the TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene annotation database. Set the TSS region to -3000 to +3000 bp. Convert the annotation result to a data frame. Calculate the distribution of peaks across genomic features (Promoter, Exon, Intron, Intergenic, etc.) by summarizing the 'annotation' column. Save the following outputs to 'outputs/': (1) 'annotated_peaks.csv' containing the full annotation table with peak locations, nearest genes, and feature assignments; and (2) 'genomic_distribution.csv' containing the count and percentage of peaks in each genomic feature category. Do not generate any plots.

### sample_peaks.bed.gz (20,893 bytes)
[Binary file: 20,893 bytes; represented here by file metadata.]
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ChIPseeker))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(clusterProfiler))

# 1. Load Data
message("1. Loading ChIP-seq peaks...")
peak_file <- file.path("inputs", "sample_peaks.bed.gz")
if (!file.exists(peak_file)) stop("Peak file not found.")

# readPeakFile reads BED files into GRanges
# This particular sample file is from hg19 (human) usually, or mm9/mm10 (mouse).
# The ChIPseeker example files are often hg19. Let's assume hg19 as we are using TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene.
# Wait, let's verify if the file "GSM1295076_CBX6_BF_ChipSeq_mergedReps_peaks.bed.gz" is human.
# CBX6 is human protein. GSM1295076 is defined as "Homo sapiens". So hg19 is appropriate.
peaks <- readPeakFile(peak_file)

# 2. Peak Annotation
message("2. Annotating peaks with genomic features...")
# annotatePeak assigns each peak to the nearest gene and genomic feature (Promoter, UTR, etc.)
# tssRegion defines the promoter region window around TSS (e.g., -3000 to +3000 bp)
txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene
peak_anno <- annotatePeak(peaks, tssRegion = c(-3000, 3000),
                         TxDb = txdb,
                         verbose = FALSE)

# 3. Extract Annotation Statistics
message("3. Extracting annotation tables...")
# Convert annotation object to data frame
peak_df <- as.data.frame(peak_anno)

# 4. Summarize Distribution
# ChIPseeker's plotAnnoPie does this visually, we calculate it numerically.
# The 'annotation' column contains the feature type (e.g., "Promoter (<=1kb)", "Intron (1 of 34)")
# We simplify these categories to main types.
feature_counts <- table(gsub(" \\(.*", "", peak_df$annotation))
feature_summary <- data.frame(
    Feature = names(feature_counts),
    Count = as.integer(feature_counts),
    Percentage = as.numeric(prop.table(feature_counts)) * 100
)
feature_summary <- feature_summary[order(-feature_summary$Count), ]

# 5. Save outputs
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save Annotations (Full Table)
# This includes chromosome residues, peak locations, and assigned genes (Entrez ID, Symbol, etc.)
write.csv(peak_df, file = file.path(output_dir, "annotated_peaks.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save Feature Distribution Summary
write.csv(feature_summary, file = file.path(output_dir, "genomic_distribution.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

message(sprintf("Analysis complete. Annotated %d peaks.", nrow(peak_df)))
message("Results saved to outputs/")

prompt: Write R code to annotate ChIP-seq peaks with nearby genes using ChIPseeker. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(ChIPseeker). The goal is to interpret which genomic features your binding sites fall into (for example, promoters, exons, or intergenic regions) and which genes they are likely to regulate, using the BED file at inputs/peaks.bed as input. Use readPeakFile() to load the peaks and then annotatePeak() with tssRegion=c(-3000,3000), TxDb=TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene, and annoDb="org.Hs.eg.db", relying only on ChIPseeker and its documented helper annotation packages rather than bringing in any additional toolkits; be sure to carry through the full annotation object without dropping fields so it can be used downstream. Save the complete csAnno object as an RDS file to outputs/annotated_peaks.rds and also export a tabular version of the annotations to outputs/peak_annotation.csv, and as a quick quality check confirm that both files are created, look at the distribution of annotation categories around TSS, and check for NA-heavy columns or obviously malformed entries in the output table.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
library(ChIPseeker)
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene)

peaks = readPeakFile('inputs/peaks.bed')
peakAnno = annotatePeak(peaks, tssRegion=c(-3000, 3000),
                        TxDb=TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene,
                        annoDb="org.Hs.eg.db")
saveRDS(peakAnno, 'outputs/annotated_peaks.rds')
write.csv(as.data.frame(peakAnno), 'outputs/peak_annotation.csv', row.names=FALSE, quote=TRUE)

Read Drosophila RNA-seq differential expression results from inputs/drosphila_example_de.csv. Prepare a sorted gene list from log2FoldChange values with ENSEMBL IDs. Run gseGO() with parameters: ont='ALL', keyType='ENSEMBL', nPerm=10000, minGSSize=3, maxGSSize=800, pvalueCutoff=0.05, pAdjustMethod='none', OrgDb=org.Dm.eg.db. suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(clusterProfiler))

set.seed(1000)

# 2. 设置生物体
organism <- "org.Dm.eg.db"
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(organism, character.only = TRUE))
orgdb <- get(organism)

# 3. 创建输出目录
output_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# 4. 检查输入文件
input_path <- file.path("inputs", "drosphila_example_de.csv")
if (!file.exists(input_path)) {
  stop("drosphila_example_de.csv is required input")
}

# 5. 读取数据
df <- read.csv(input_path, header = TRUE)

# 6. 准备基因列表
original_gene_list <- df$log2FoldChange
names(original_gene_list) <- df$gene_id
gene_list <- na.omit(original_gene_list)

    stop("Input file 'inputs/gene_list.txt' not found.")
}

set.seed(1000)

# 2. 检查输入文件
data_path <- file.path("inputs", "data.csv")
design_path <- file.path("inputs", "experimental_design.csv")

if (!file.exists(data_path) || !file.exists(design_path)) {
  stop("data.csv and experimental_design.csv are required inputs")
}

# 3. 创建输出目录
outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# 4. 读取和处理数据
data <- read.csv(data_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = TRUE)
data <- filter(
  data,
  is.na(Reverse) | Reverse != "+",
  is.na(Potential.contaminant) | Potential.contaminant != "+"
)

# 5. 生成唯一基因名
data_unique <- make_unique(data, "Gene.names", "Protein.IDs", delim = ";")

# 6. 准备实验设计和SummarizedExperiment对象
LFQ_columns <- grep("^LFQ\\.intensity\\.", colnames(data_unique))
labels <- sub("^LFQ\\.intensity\\.", "", colnames(data_unique)[LFQ_columns])
experimental_design <- data.frame(
  label = labels,
  condition = sub("_[0-9]+$", "", labels),
  replicate = as.integer(sub("^.*_", "", labels)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
data_se <- make_se(data_unique, LFQ_columns, experimental_design)

# 7. 数据质量控制
data_filt <- filter_missval(data_se, thr = 1)
data_norm <- normalize_vsn(data_filt)

# 8. 缺失值插补
data_imp <- impute(data_norm, fun = "MinProb", q = 0.01)

# 9. 保存输出结果
saveRDS(data_imp, file.path(outputs_dir, "DataForDEP.rds"))

prompt: Perform RNA-seq differential expression analysis using DESeq2. Load DESeq2 package. Read inputs/counts.csv (count matrix) and inputs/colData.csv (sample information). Filter genes with mean count > 5. Create DESeqDataSet with design ~conditions. Run DESeq() for differential analysis. Filter results with padj<0.05 and |log2FC|>1. Annotate genes as 'Up', 'Down', or 'NotSig'. Save all results to outputs/DEG_results.csv.
solution_r:
# 1. 加载包
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(DESeq2))

# 2. 检查输入文件
counts_path <- file.path("inputs", "counts.csv")
coldata_path <- file.path("inputs", "colData.csv")

if (!file.exists(counts_path) || !file.exists(coldata_path)) {
  stop("counts.csv and colData.csv are required inputs")
}

# 3. 创建输出目录
outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# 4. 读取数据
count_df <- read.csv(counts_path, check.names = FALSE)
wt.raw.counts <- rowsum(as.matrix(count_df[, -1, drop = FALSE]), group = count_df[[1]])
colData <- read.csv(coldata_path, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
colData <- colData[colnames(wt.raw.counts), , drop = FALSE]

# 5. 过滤低表达基因
wt.filtered.counts <- wt.raw.counts[rowMeans(wt.raw.counts) > 5, ]

# 6. DESeq2差异分析
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(wt.filtered.counts, colData, design = ~conditions)
dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- results(dds)

# 7. 筛选差异基因

res.df$group <- "NotSig"

res.df$group[res.df$padj < 0.05 & res.df$log2FoldChange < -1] <- "Down"

prompt: Perform a differential expression analysis using the DESeq2 package in R. First, load the required package. Read the raw count matrix from 'inputs/counts.tsv' (tab-separated, header=TRUE, row.names=1) and the sample metadata from 'inputs/col_data.tsv' (tab-separated, header=TRUE, row.names=1). Ensure that the column names of the count matrix align exactly with the row names of the metadata; if there are mismatches, intersect the sample names to keep only common samples and reorder the count matrix columns to match the metadata rows. In the metadata, convert the 'dex' column to a factor and strictly set the reference level to 'untrt' (control group). Create a DESeqDataSet object using `DESeqDataSetFromMatrix` with the design formula `~ dex`. Run the standard DESeq2 pipeline using the `DESeq()` function. Extract the results for the specific contrast comparing 'trt' (treated) vs 'untrt' (untreated). Order the result table by adjusted p-value (ascending). Save the full ordered results to 'outputs/results_full.csv'. additionally, subset the results to keep only genes with an adjusted p-value (padj) less than 0.1, and save this subset to 'outputs/results_sig.csv'. Finally, save the processed DESeqDataSet object as an RDS file to 'outputs/dds.rds'. Ensure the code is robust to missing files by checking for their existence first.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(DESeq2))

# 1. Load input data
counts_file <- file.path("inputs", "counts.tsv")
col_data_file <- file.path("inputs", "col_data.tsv")

if (!file.exists(counts_file) || !file.exists(col_data_file)) {
    stop("Input files not found.")
}

# Read counts: first column is gene names, check.names=FALSE to preserve sample names
counts_mat <- read.table(counts_file, header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE)

# Read coldata, check.names=FALSE
col_data <- read.table(col_data_file, header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# 2. Check and align samples
# Ensure columns of counts_mat match rows of col_data
common_samples <- intersect(colnames(counts_mat), rownames(col_data))

if (length(common_samples) == 0) {
    stop("No matching samples found between counts and metadata.")
}

counts_mat <- as.matrix(counts_mat[, common_samples, drop = FALSE])
col_data <- col_data[common_samples, , drop = FALSE]

# align columns of counts with rows of coldata
# This is critical for DESeq2
# Also ensure 'dex' is a factor with reference level 'untrt'
if ("dex" %in% colnames(col_data)) {
    col_data$dex <- factor(col_data$dex)
    col_data$dex <- relevel(col_data$dex, ref = "untrt")
} else {
    stop("Column 'dex' not found in metadata.")
}

# 3. Create DESeqDataSet object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts_mat,
                              colData = col_data,
                              design = ~ dex)

# 4. Run DESeq analysis
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# 5. Extract results
# Contrast: dex, trt vs untrt
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("dex", "trt", "untrt"))

# Order by p-value
res_ordered <- res[order(res$padj), ]

# 6. Save outputs
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save full results as CSV
write.csv(as.data.frame(res_ordered), file.path(output_dir, "results_full.csv"))

# Save significant results (padj < 0.1) as CSV
res_sig <- subset(res_ordered, padj < 0.1)
write.csv(as.data.frame(res_sig), file.path(output_dir, "results_sig.csv"))

# Save processed DESeq object as RDS
saveRDS(dds, file.path(output_dir, "dds.rds"))

message("Analysis complete. Results saved to outputs/")

prompt: Write R code to summarize gene-wise expression variability using genefilter. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(genefilter). You will work from the gene expression count matrix at inputs/counts.tsv, reading it into R, converting it to a numeric matrix, then computing per-gene means with rowMeans, standard deviations with rowSds, and coefficients of variation as rowSds divided by rowMeans while handling genes with zero mean in a sensible way (for example, avoiding division by zero). Using only genefilter and its documented helpers, assemble these results into a data frame with columns gene, mean_expression, sd_expression, and cv, sort the rows by decreasing sd_expression, write the full table to outputs/gene_statistics.csv, and then extract the top 100 most variable genes by sd_expression and save them as outputs/top_variable_genes.csv in CSV format. At the end, quickly confirm that both CSV files were created, inspect basic summary statistics for the mean and standard deviation distributions, and check that you are not generating excessive NA values or clearly implausible outliers.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(genefilter))

counts_path <- file.path("inputs", "counts.tsv")
if (!file.exists(counts_path)) {
  stop("counts.tsv is required")
}

expr_df <- read.delim(counts_path, check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
expr_mat <- as.matrix(expr_df)

row_means <- rowMeans(expr_mat)
row_sds <- rowSds(expr_mat)
cv <- ifelse(row_means == 0, NA_real_, row_sds / row_means)

stats <- data.frame(
  gene = rownames(expr_mat),
  mean_expression = row_means,
  sd_expression = row_sds,
  cv = cv,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
stats <- stats[order(-stats$sd_expression), ]

top_n <- min(100, nrow(stats))
top_genes <- stats[seq_len(top_n), ]

outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(stats, file.path(outputs_dir, "gene_statistics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(top_genes, file.path(outputs_dir, "top_variable_genes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

prompt: Write R code to perform row-wise two-sample t-tests for differential gene expression between two groups using genefilter. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(genefilter). You should start from the expression matrix in inputs/counts.tsv, treat the first half of the columns as GroupA and the remaining columns as GroupB, convert the data to a matrix with genes as rows, and then use genefilter::rowttests to obtain the t-statistics and p-values for each gene. For each gene, also compute the mean expression in GroupA and GroupB and derive a group_difference value as GroupA mean minus GroupB mean, then assemble a results table with columns gene, statistic, pvalue, and group_difference, sorted first by increasing pvalue and then by the absolute t-statistic, and write this to outputs/differential_expression.csv as a comma-separated file; in addition, create a small summary table with total_genes and significant_genes (p < 0.05) and save it to outputs/ttest_summary.csv. Please rely only on genefilter and base R functionality to carry out this analysis, without adding other analysis packages. As a basic quality control step, confirm that both CSV files are created, quickly inspect the distributions of p-values and group_difference values, and check for unexpected NA-heavy output or signs that the samples were misassigned between GroupA and GroupB.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(genefilter))

counts_path <- file.path("inputs", "counts.tsv")
if (!file.exists(counts_path)) {
  stop("counts.tsv is required for rowttests")
}

expr_df <- read.delim(counts_path, check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
expr_mat <- as.matrix(expr_df)

n_samples <- ncol(expr_mat)
if (n_samples < 2) {
  stop("Need at least two samples for a t-test")
}

split_point <- ceiling(n_samples / 2)
groups <- rep("GroupB", n_samples)
groups[seq_len(split_point)] <- "GroupA"
groups <- factor(groups, levels = c("GroupA", "GroupB"))

res <- rowttests(expr_mat, groups)
mean_groupA <- rowMeans(expr_mat[, groups == "GroupA", drop = FALSE])
mean_groupB <- rowMeans(expr_mat[, groups == "GroupB", drop = FALSE])

diff_expr <- data.frame(
  gene = rownames(expr_mat),
  statistic = res$statistic,
  pvalue = res$p.value,
  group_difference = mean_groupA - mean_groupB,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
diff_expr <- diff_expr[order(diff_expr$pvalue, -abs(diff_expr$statistic)), ]

sig_count <- sum(diff_expr$pvalue < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
summary_df <- data.frame(
  total_genes = nrow(diff_expr),
  significant_genes = sig_count
)

outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(diff_expr, file.path(outputs_dir, "differential_expression.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(summary_df, file.path(outputs_dir, "ttest_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

prompt: Write R code to perform gene-level ROC/AUC discrimination between two sample groups using genefilter. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(genefilter). Starting from the gene expression count matrix in inputs/counts.tsv, where rows are genes and columns are samples, treat the first half of the samples as GroupA (positives) and the remaining samples as GroupB (negatives), convert the data to a numeric matrix, and use the genefilter::rowpAUCs function with parameters such as p = 1 and flip = FALSE to compute per-gene AUC values that quantify how well each gene separates the two groups. From these results, construct a data frame with one row per gene that includes the gene identifier, its AUC, and a direction label indicating whether GroupA>GroupB or GroupB>GroupA based on whether the AUC is above or below 0.5, then write this table as a CSV file to outputs/rowroc_results.csv; in addition, create a small summary table with the total number of genes and the count of genes with AUC at least 0.75 and save it as outputs/roc_summary.csv. Please rely only on genefilter and its documented helper functions for all steps of this analysis, and as a basic quality control step confirm that both CSV outputs are created, briefly review the AUC distribution and summary counts for biological plausibility, and check for excessive NA values or other anomalies in the results.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(genefilter))

counts_path <- file.path("inputs", "counts.tsv")
if (!file.exists(counts_path)) stop("counts.tsv missing")
expr_df <- read.delim(counts_path, check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
expr_mat <- as.matrix(expr_df)

n_samples <- ncol(expr_mat)
if (n_samples < 2) stop("Need >=2 samples")
mid <- ceiling(n_samples / 2)
labels <- factor(c(rep("GroupA", mid), rep("GroupB", n_samples - mid)))

roc_obj <- rowpAUCs(expr_mat, labels, p = 1, flip = FALSE)
auc_vals <- slot(roc_obj, "AUC")
direction <- ifelse(auc_vals >= 0.5, "GroupA>GroupB", "GroupB>GroupA")

results <- data.frame(
  gene = rownames(expr_mat),
  AUC = auc_vals,
  direction = direction,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

summary_df <- data.frame(
  total_genes = nrow(results),
  auc_ge_0_75 = sum(results$AUC >= 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
)

outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(results, file.path(outputs_dir, "rowroc_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(summary_df, file.path(outputs_dir, "roc_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

prompt: Using R and the graph package, read the numeric feature matrix from `inputs/matrix.tsv`. Compute pairwise Pearson correlations between columns with pairwise-complete observations, use their absolute values as weights, set the diagonal to zero, and create an undirected `graphAM` containing every nonzero association. solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(graph))

matrix_path <- file.path("inputs", "matrix.tsv")
mat <- read.delim(matrix_path, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE)
if (ncol(mat) < 2) {
  stop("matrix.tsv needs at least two columns")
}

corr <- cor(mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
weights <- abs(corr)
diag(weights) <- 0
adj_mat <- ifelse(weights > 0, 1, 0)

graph_obj <- graphAM(adjMat = adj_mat, values = list(weight = weights), edgemode = "undirected")

deg <- rowSums(unweighted)

  node = node_names,
  degree = deg,
  weighted_degree = weighted_degree,
  clustering_coeff = clustering,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

prompt: Write R code to construct a correlation-based undirected network and summarize each node’s neighborhood using graph. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(graph). The input is a numeric matrix at inputs/matrix.tsv, representing features such as genes or metabolites measured across samples, and the goal is to identify strongly co-varying pairs that may reflect shared regulation or common pathways. Read this matrix, compute the pairwise Pearson correlation between all columns, convert correlations to absolute values, set self-correlations to zero, and threshold the resulting matrix at an absolute correlation of at least 0.6 before using graph::graphAM to build an undirected graph; then, with graph helpers like edgeWeights and nodes, extract each node’s neighbors and their correlation weights to produce a detailed edge list written to outputs/neighbors.csv and a separate summary table with node, degree, and average_weight written to outputs/neighbor_summary.csv, both as CSV files. Please rely only on the graph package together with base R functions (do not introduce other network analysis toolkits), and as a basic quality check confirm that both CSVs are created, inspect that degrees and average weights are biologically plausible and not dominated by NAs or empty neighborhoods, and verify that the correlation thresholding behaved as expected.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(graph))

matrix_path <- file.path("inputs", "matrix.tsv")
if (!file.exists(matrix_path)) stop("matrix.tsv missing")
mat <- read.delim(matrix_path, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE)
corr <- cor(mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
weights <- abs(corr)
weights[is.na(weights)] <- 0
diag(weights) <- 0
adj <- ifelse(weights >= 0.6, 1, 0)
nodes <- colnames(mat)
colnames(adj) <- rownames(adj) <- nodes

graph_obj <- graphAM(adjMat = adj, values = list(weight = weights), edgemode = "undirected")
edge_map <- edgeWeights(graph_obj)

records <- list()
for (nd in nodes(graph_obj)) {
  nbrs <- names(edge_map[[nd]])
  if (length(nbrs) == 0) next
  rec <- data.frame(
    node = nd,
    neighbor = nbrs,
    weight = as.numeric(edge_map[[nd]]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  records[[nd]] <- rec
}
neighbor_df <- if (length(records)) do.call(rbind, records) else data.frame(node = character(), neighbor = character(), weight = numeric())

if (nrow(neighbor_df) == 0) {
  summary_df <- data.frame(node = nodes(graph_obj), degree = 0, average_weight = 0)
} else {
  avg_df <- aggregate(weight ~ node, data = neighbor_df, FUN = mean)
  deg_df <- aggregate(neighbor ~ node, data = neighbor_df, FUN = length)
  colnames(deg_df) <- c("node", "degree")
  colnames(avg_df) <- c("node", "average_weight")
  summary_df <- merge(deg_df, avg_df, by = "node", all = TRUE)
  all_nodes <- data.frame(node = nodes(graph_obj))
  summary_df <- merge(all_nodes, summary_df, by = "node", all.x = TRUE)
  summary_df$degree[is.na(summary_df$degree)] <- 0
  summary_df$average_weight[is.na(summary_df$average_weight)] <- 0
}

outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(neighbor_df, file.path(outputs_dir, "neighbors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(summary_df, file.path(outputs_dir, "neighbor_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

prompt: Using graph, read `inputs/matrix.tsv`, compute pairwise-complete Pearson correlations between columns, replace missing values with zero, take absolute values, zero the diagonal, and connect pairs with weight at least 0.5 in an undirected graph. Find connected components with `connComp`. Label components `C1`, `C2`, and so on; write each `node` and `component_id` to `outputs/component_nodes.csv`, and write each `component_id` and `size` to `outputs/component_sizes.csv`.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(graph))

matrix_path <- file.path("inputs", "matrix.tsv")
if (!file.exists(matrix_path)) stop("matrix.tsv missing")
mat <- read.delim(matrix_path, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE)
corr <- cor(mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
abs_corr <- abs(corr)
abs_corr[is.na(abs_corr)] <- 0
diag(abs_corr) <- 0
threshold <- 0.5
adj <- ifelse(abs_corr >= threshold, 1, 0)
nodes <- colnames(mat)
colnames(adj) <- rownames(adj) <- nodes

g <- graphAM(adjMat = adj, values = list(weight = abs_corr), edgemode = "undirected")
components <- connComp(as(g, "graphNEL"))
component_nodes <- list()
component_sizes <- data.frame(component_id = character(), size = integer(0), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for (i in seq_along(components)) {
  comp_id <- paste0("C", i)
  nodes_in_comp <- components[[i]]
  component_nodes[[i]] <- data.frame(node = nodes_in_comp, component_id = comp_id, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  component_sizes <- rbind(component_sizes, data.frame(component_id = comp_id, size = length(nodes_in_comp), stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}
node_df <- if (length(component_nodes)) do.call(rbind, component_nodes) else data.frame(node = character(), component_id = character())
outputs_dir <- "outputs"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(node_df, file.path(outputs_dir, "component_nodes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(component_sizes, file.path(outputs_dir, "component_sizes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(GSEABase))

gmt_path <- file.path('inputs', 'signature.gmt')
if (!file.exists(gmt_path)) stop('signature.gmt input is missing.')

gsc <- getGmt(gmt_path)
if (length(gsc) == 0) stop('GeneSetCollection is empty.')

all_genes <- unlist(geneIds(gsc), use.names = FALSE)
if (length(all_genes) == 0) stop('No genes found in gene sets.')

gene_counts <- sort(table(all_genes), decreasing = TRUE)
target_gene <- names(gene_counts)[1]

contains_gene <- vapply(gsc, function(gs) target_gene %in% geneIds(gs), logical(1))
if (!any(contains_gene)) {
  stop('Target gene was not found in any gene set.')
}

subset_collection <- gsc[contains_gene]
set_sizes <- vapply(gsc, function(gs) length(geneIds(gs)), integer(1))

membership_df <- data.frame(
  set_name = names(gsc),
  contains_gene = contains_gene,
  set_size = set_sizes,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
saveRDS(subset_collection, file.path('outputs', 'subset_collection.rds'))
write.csv(membership_df, file.path('outputs', 'gene_membership.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

gmt_path <- file.path('inputs', 'signature.gmt')
if (!file.exists(gmt_path)) stop('signature.gmt input is missing.')

gsc <- getGmt(gmt_path)
sizes <- vapply(gsc, function(gs) length(geneIds(gs)), integer(1))
if (length(sizes) == 0) stop('GeneSetCollection is empty.')

quartiles <- quantile(sizes, probs = c(0.25, 0.75))
lower <- as.numeric(quartiles[[1]])
upper <- as.numeric(quartiles[[2]])
within_range <- sizes >= lower & sizes <= upper

if (!any(within_range)) {
  target <- order(abs(sizes - median(sizes)))[1:max(1, ceiling(length(sizes) * 0.6))]
  within_range <- seq_along(sizes) %in% target
}

filtered_collection <- gsc[within_range]
summary_df <- data.frame(
  set_name = names(gsc),
  size = sizes,
  within_iqr = within_range,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
saveRDS(filtered_collection, file.path('outputs', 'filtered_collection.rds'))
write.csv(summary_df, file.path('outputs', 'filtered_sets.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(GSEABase))

gmt_path <- file.path('inputs', 'signature.gmt')
if (!file.exists(gmt_path)) stop('signature.gmt input is missing.')

gsc <- getGmt(gmt_path)
if (length(gsc) == 0) stop('GeneSetCollection is empty.')

inc_mat <- incidence(gsc)
inc_mat <- as.matrix(inc_mat)

overlap_mat <- t(inc_mat) %*% inc_mat
overlap_df <- as.data.frame(overlap_mat)
overlap_df <- cbind(set_name = rownames(overlap_mat), overlap_df)

set_names <- rownames(overlap_mat)
summary_list <- lapply(seq_along(set_names), function(i) {
  row_vals <- overlap_mat[i, ]
  row_vals[i] <- NA
  partner_idx <- which.max(row_vals)
  if (length(partner_idx) == 0 || is.na(row_vals[partner_idx])) {
    partner_name <- NA_character_
    overlap_size <- 0
  } else {
    partner_name <- set_names[partner_idx]
    overlap_size <- as.numeric(row_vals[partner_idx])
  }
  data.frame(
    set_name = set_names[i],
    best_partner = partner_name,
    overlap_size = overlap_size,
    self_size = diag(overlap_mat)[i],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

overlap_summary <- do.call(rbind, summary_list)

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(overlap_df, file.path('outputs', 'overlap_matrix.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(overlap_summary, file.path('outputs', 'overlap_summary.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(GSEABase))

gmt_path <- file.path('inputs', 'signature.gmt')
if (!file.exists(gmt_path)) stop('signature.gmt input is missing.')

gsc <- getGmt(gmt_path)
sizes <- vapply(gsc, function(gs) length(geneIds(gs)), integer(1))
if (length(sizes) < 2) stop('Need at least two gene sets to compare.')

order_idx <- order(sizes, decreasing = TRUE)
set_a <- gsc[[order_idx[1]]]
set_b <- gsc[[order_idx[2]]]

genes_a <- geneIds(set_a)
genes_b <- geneIds(set_b)

union_genes <- sort(unique(c(genes_a, genes_b)))
intersection_genes <- sort(intersect(genes_a, genes_b))
unique_a <- setdiff(genes_a, genes_b)
unique_b <- setdiff(genes_b, genes_a)

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(union_genes, con = file.path('outputs', 'union_genes.txt'))
writeLines(intersection_genes, con = file.path('outputs', 'intersection_genes.txt'))

summary_df <- data.frame(
  set_name = c(names(gsc)[order_idx[1]], names(gsc)[order_idx[2]]),
  size = c(length(genes_a), length(genes_b)),
  unique_genes = c(length(unique_a), length(unique_b)),
  intersection_size = length(intersection_genes),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
write.csv(summary_df, file.path('outputs', 'comparison_summary.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(GSEABase))

gmt_path <- file.path('inputs', 'signature.gmt')
if (!file.exists(gmt_path)) stop('signature.gmt input is missing.')

gsc <- getGmt(gmt_path)
if (length(gsc) == 0) stop('GeneSetCollection is empty.')

sizes <- vapply(gsc, function(gs) length(geneIds(gs)), integer(1))
order_idx <- order(sizes, decreasing = TRUE)
keep_n <- min(5, length(order_idx))
top_idx <- order_idx[seq_len(keep_n)]
top_collection <- gsc[top_idx]

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
toGmt(top_collection, file.path('outputs', 'top_sets.gmt'))

metadata <- data.frame(
  rank = seq_len(keep_n),
  set_name = names(gsc)[top_idx],
  size = sizes[top_idx],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
write.csv(metadata, file.path('outputs', 'top_sets_metadata.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(GSEABase))

gmt_path <- file.path('inputs', 'signature.gmt')
if (!file.exists(gmt_path)) stop('signature.gmt input is missing.')

gsc <- getGmt(gmt_path)
if (length(gsc) == 0) stop('GeneSetCollection is empty.')

inc_mat <- incidence(gsc)
inc_mat <- as.matrix(inc_mat)

membership_df <- data.frame(gene = rownames(inc_mat), inc_mat, check.names = FALSE)
all_genes <- unlist(geneIds(gsc), use.names = FALSE)
gene_counts <- sort(table(all_genes), decreasing = TRUE)
gene_counts_df <- data.frame(
  gene = names(gene_counts),
  set_count = as.integer(gene_counts),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.table(membership_df, file = file.path('outputs', 'membership_matrix.tsv'), sep = '	', row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
write.csv(gene_counts_df, file.path('outputs', 'gene_counts.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(GSEABase))

gmt_path <- file.path('inputs', 'signature.gmt')
if (!file.exists(gmt_path)) stop('signature.gmt input is missing.')

gsc <- getGmt(gmt_path)
set_names <- names(gsc)
sizes <- vapply(gsc, function(gs) length(geneIds(gs)), integer(1))

prefixes <- vapply(set_names, function(nm) {
  parts <- strsplit(nm, '_', fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (length(parts) == 0) nm else parts[1]
}, character(1))

groups_df <- data.frame(
  set_name = set_names,
  prefix = prefixes,
  size = sizes,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

summary_df <- aggregate(
  list(n_sets = groups_df$size),
  by = list(prefix = groups_df$prefix),
  FUN = length
)
summary_sizes <- aggregate(
  list(mean_size = groups_df$size),
  by = list(prefix = groups_df$prefix),
  FUN = mean
)
summary_df <- merge(summary_df, summary_sizes, by = 'prefix')

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(groups_df, file.path('outputs', 'prefix_groups.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(summary_df, file.path('outputs', 'prefix_summary.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(GSEABase))

gmt_path <- file.path('inputs', 'signature.gmt')
if (!file.exists(gmt_path)) stop('signature.gmt input is missing.')

gsc <- getGmt(gmt_path)
if (length(gsc) == 0) stop('GeneSetCollection is empty.')

all_genes <- unique(unlist(geneIds(gsc), use.names = FALSE))
total_unique <- length(all_genes)

stat_list <- lapply(seq_along(gsc), function(i) {
  gs <- gsc[[i]]
  genes <- sort(geneIds(gs))
  data.frame(
    set_name = names(gsc)[i],
    size = length(genes),
    unique_gene_fraction = if (total_unique == 0) NA_real_ else length(genes) / total_unique,
    first_gene = if (length(genes) == 0) NA_character_ else genes[1],
    last_gene = if (length(genes) == 0) NA_character_ else genes[length(genes)],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

stat_df <- do.call(rbind, stat_list)
collection_summary <- data.frame(
  total_sets = length(gsc),
  total_unique_genes = total_unique,
  median_set_size = stats::median(stat_df$size),
  mean_set_size = mean(stat_df$size),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(stat_df, file.path('outputs', 'set_statistics.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(collection_summary, file.path('outputs', 'collection_summary.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(GSEABase))

gmt_path <- file.path('inputs', 'signature.gmt')
if (!file.exists(gmt_path)) stop('signature.gmt input is missing.')

gsc <- getGmt(gmt_path)
if (length(gsc) == 0) stop('GeneSetCollection is empty.')

set.seed(123)
set_names <- names(gsc)
n_sets <- length(set_names)
train_size <- max(1, floor(n_sets * 0.6))
train_names <- sample(set_names, train_size)

train_collection <- gsc[train_names]
eval_names <- setdiff(set_names, train_names)
eval_collection <- gsc[eval_names]

split_df <- data.frame(
  set_name = set_names,
  partition = ifelse(set_names %in% train_names, 'train', 'eval'),
  size = vapply(gsc, function(gs) length(geneIds(gs)), integer(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
saveRDS(train_collection, file.path('outputs', 'train_collection.rds'))
saveRDS(eval_collection, file.path('outputs', 'eval_collection.rds'))
write.csv(split_df, file.path('outputs', 'split_summary.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

prompt: Perform Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA). Load the expression matrix from 'inputs/expression_matrix.csv' (Rows=EntrezIDs, Cols=Samples), clinical parameters from 'inputs/metadata.csv', and molecular pathways from 'inputs/gene_sets.gmt'. Filter the GMT file down to pathways containing at least 5 genes matching exactly to your expression matrix rows. Create a GSVA parameter object utilizing 'gsvaParam()' mapping the expression array and filtered gene set paths (set minSize=5, maxSize=500). Execute 'gsva()' with this config. Following the score generation, identify differential biological features between two clinical groups: 'ALL' and 'MLL'. Perform row-wise classical t-tests on the output enrichment score matrix and compute FDR. Output the computed enrichment matrix precisely to 'outputs/gsva_enrichment_scores_matrix.csv'. Save the derived statistics sorting by most significant (P_Value) containing 'Pathway', 'Mean_Score_ALL', 'Mean_Score_MLL', 'Delta_Score', 'P_Value', and 'FDR' dynamically mapped into 'outputs/differential_pathways.csv'. Disable plot generation rendering pure computational tabular results.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(GSVA))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(stats))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(GSEABase))

# 1. Load Expression Data
message("1. Loading expression data and phenotypes...")
expr_file <- file.path("inputs", "expression_matrix.csv")
meta_file <- file.path("inputs", "metadata.csv")
gmt_file <- file.path("inputs", "gene_sets.gmt")

if (!file.exists(expr_file) || !file.exists(meta_file) || !file.exists(gmt_file)) {
    stop("Input files not found.")
}

# Read Expression matrix (Rows=Genes, Cols=Samples)
edata <- read.csv(expr_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
edata <- as.matrix(edata)

# Read Phenotype/Metadata (Rows=Samples)
pheno <- read.csv(meta_file, row.names = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# 2. Parse GMT Gene Sets manually into a named list
message("2. Loading standard gene set pathways...")
lines <- readLines(gmt_file)
gene_sets <- list()
for (line in lines) {
    parts <- strsplit(line, "\t")[[1]]
    pathway_name <- parts[1]
    # Field 2 is description/source, from 3 onwards are genes
    genes <- parts[3:length(parts)]
    # Keep only genes actually present in the expression matrix to prevent zero-length sets
    genes_present <- intersect(genes, rownames(edata))
    if (length(genes_present) >= 5) {
        gene_sets[[pathway_name]] <- genes_present
    }
}
message(sprintf("Retained %d biologically valid pathways with at least 5 matching genes.", length(gene_sets)))

if (length(gene_sets) == 0) {
    stop("No pathways had enough genes intersecting with the expression matrix.")
}

# 3. Perform Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA)
# Standard formulation for newer GSVA packages (> 1.50) using gsvaParam
message("3. Executing GSVA (Single-sample non-parametric pathway enrichment)...")
gsvapar <- gsvaParam(exprData = edata, 
                     geneSets = gene_sets, 
                     minSize = 5, 
                     maxSize = 500)

gsva_results <- gsva(gsvapar, verbose = FALSE)

# 4. Numerically Evaluate Pathway Differences
message("4. Computing differential pathway activation (ALL vs MLL)...")
# GSVA outputs a matrix of enrichment scores (Rows=Pathways, Cols=Samples)
# We can run parametric tests (t-tests) since GSVA scores approximate normal distributions

is_ALL <- pheno$Subtype == "ALL"
is_MLL <- pheno$Subtype == "MLL"

diff_pathway_table <- data.frame(
    Pathway = rownames(gsva_results),
    Mean_Score_ALL = rowMeans(gsva_results[, is_ALL], na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Score_MLL = rowMeans(gsva_results[, is_MLL], na.rm = TRUE),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
diff_pathway_table$Delta_Score <- diff_pathway_table$Mean_Score_ALL - diff_pathway_table$Mean_Score_MLL

# Perform row-wise T-tests 
p_values <- numeric(nrow(gsva_results))
for (i in 1:nrow(gsva_results)) {
    row_scores <- gsva_results[i, ]

prompt: Using gtools, read the `value` column from `inputs/values.csv` and divide it into four quantile groups with `quantcut(values, q = 4)`. Derive each factor level's lower and upper empirical quantile breaks, then write one row per original value with columns `bin`, `value`, `lower`, and `upper` to `outputs/quantile_bins.csv`, preserving input-row order within the merge behavior and omitting row names.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(gtools))

values_df <- read.csv(file.path('inputs', 'values.csv'))
if (!'value' %in% names(values_df)) stop('values.csv missing value column')
values <- values_df$value
if (length(values) < 4) stop('Need more values for quantile binning')

bins <- quantcut(values, q = 4)
level_strings <- levels(bins)
breaks <- quantile(values, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = length(level_strings) + 1), na.rm = TRUE)
interval_df <- data.frame(
  bin = factor(level_strings, levels = level_strings),
  lower = breaks[-length(breaks)],
  upper = breaks[-1]
)

result <- merge(
  data.frame(value = values, bin = bins),
  interval_df,
  by = 'bin',
  all.x = TRUE,
  sort = FALSE
)

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(result, file.path('outputs', 'quantile_bins.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(gtools))

mat <- read.table(file.path('inputs', 'matrix.tsv'), header = TRUE, sep = '\t')
cols <- c('GroupA', 'GroupB', 'GroupC', 'GroupD')
missing <- setdiff(cols, colnames(mat))
if (length(missing) > 0) stop(sprintf('Missing columns: %s', paste(missing, collapse = ',')))
data_mat <- as.matrix(mat[, cols, drop = FALSE])
col_means <- colMeans(data_mat)

  column = cols,
  mean_original = col_means,
  sd_original = apply(data_mat, 2, sd),
  mean_centered = colMeans(centered),
  sd_centered = apply(centered, 2, sd)
)

dir.create('outputs', showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

prompt: Use maftools to read inputs/mutations.maf. Rank genes using getGeneSummary(), retain the first 10 genes, and filter the MAF to those genes with filterMaf(). Write the filtered mutation table to outputs/filtered.maf as a tab-separated file without row names or quotes.
solution_r:
library(maftools)

# Read MAF file
maf <- read.maf('inputs/mutations.maf', verbose = FALSE)

# Get list of genes in MAF
all_genes <- getGeneSummary(maf)$Hugo_Symbol

# Select subset of genes for filtering (e.g., top 10 most mutated)
genes_to_keep <- head(all_genes, 10)

# Filter MAF to keep only selected genes
filtered_maf <- filterMaf(maf, genes = genes_to_keep)

# Write filtered MAF
write.table(filtered_maf@data, 'outputs/filtered.maf', sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

library(maftools)

# Read MAF file
maf <- read.maf('inputs/mutations.maf', verbose = FALSE)

# Get list of all samples
all_samples <- getSampleSummary(maf)$Tumor_Sample_Barcode

solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Analyze somatic gene interactions from mutation data
# Identifies co-occurring and mutually exclusive gene mutations

library(maftools)

# Read MAF (Mutation Annotation Format) file
maf <- read.maf('inputs/mutations.maf', verbose = FALSE)

# Calculate somatic interactions between mutated genes
# top = 10: analyze top 10 most mutated genes
# pvalue = c(0.05, 0.05): significance thresholds for co-occurrence and mutual exclusivity
# returnAll = TRUE: return all pairwise comparisons
# plotMatrix = FALSE: don't generate plot, just return data
interactions <- somaticInteractions(maf, top = 10, pvalue = c(0.05, 0.05), returnAll = TRUE)

# Save interaction results to CSV
write.csv(interactions, 'outputs/interactions.csv', row.names = FALSE)

prompt: Perform CpG-level DNA methylation analysis. Load unmethylated (U) ('inputs/unmethylated_signals.csv') and methylated (M) ('inputs/methylated_signals.csv') intensity signals along with metadata ('inputs/metadata.csv'). First, convert these raw intensities into biologically interpretable 'Beta values' (M / (M + U + 100)) and statistically robust 'M-values' (log2((M+1)/(U+1))). Save these generated coordinate matrices to 'outputs/beta_values_matrix.csv' and 'outputs/m_values_matrix.csv' respectively. Second, conduct a site-wise classical T-Test between 'cancer' and 'normal' groups (defined in metadata 'Status') using the M-values to determine statistical significance. Calculate numerical difference (Delta_Beta = mean(cancer_beta) - mean(normal_beta)). Finally, output 'outputs/differential_methylation_stats.csv' containing precisely 'Probe_ID', 'Mean_Beta_Cancer', 'Mean_Beta_Normal', 'Delta_Beta', 'P_Value', and 'FDR'. Disable visual plot generation.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(minfi))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(stats))

# 1. Load Data
message("1. Loading raw methylation signals...")
M_file <- file.path("inputs", "methylated_signals.csv")
U_file <- file.path("inputs", "unmethylated_signals.csv")
meta_file <- file.path("inputs", "metadata.csv")

if (!file.exists(M_file) || !file.exists(U_file)) stop("Methylation signal files not found.")

# Read matrices
# M: Methylated signal strength, U: Unmethylated signal strength
mat_M <- as.matrix(read.csv(M_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
mat_U <- as.matrix(read.csv(U_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
pheno <- read.csv(meta_file, row.names = 1)

# Ensure data alignment
if (!identical(dim(mat_M), dim(mat_U)) || !identical(colnames(mat_M), rownames(pheno))) {
    stop("Data dimensions or sample names do not match perfectly.")
}

# 2. Compute Metric Arrays (Beta and M-values)
message("2. Calculating Beta values and M-values...")

# Offset prevents division by zero
offset <- 100 
# Beta value: Ratio of methylated to total signal [0, 1] 
# Biologically interpretable (0.5 means 50% methylated cells)
Beta_values <- mat_M / (mat_M + mat_U + offset)

# M value: Log2 ratio of Methylated to Unmethylated intensities
# Statistically superior for downstream differential analysis (homoscedasticity)
# Small offset prevents log2(0)
M_values <- log2((mat_M + 1) / (mat_U + 1))

# 3. Simple Differential Methylation Probing
message("3. Performing site-wise differential calculation (Cancer vs Normal)...")

# Define groups
is_cancer <- pheno$Status == "cancer"
is_normal <- pheno$Status == "normal"

# Compute means per group (for Beta values) to find absolute delta-beta
mean_Beta_cancer <- rowMeans(Beta_values[, is_cancer], na.rm = TRUE)
mean_Beta_normal <- rowMeans(Beta_values[, is_normal], na.rm = TRUE)
delta_Beta <- mean_Beta_cancer - mean_Beta_normal

# Simple t-test using M-values (Statistically rigorous method)
p_values <- numeric(nrow(M_values))
for (i in 1:nrow(M_values)) {
    # Extract row
    row_M <- M_values[i, ]
    # t.test requires variance, so check if we have enough points
    if(sum(!is.na(row_M)) >= 3) {
        test <- tryCatch(
            t.test(row_M[is_cancer], row_M[is_normal]), 
            error = function(e) list(p.value = NA)
        )
        p_values[i] <- test$p.value
    } else {
        p_values[i] <- NA
    }
}

# Adjust p-values for multiple comparisons (False Discovery Rate)
fdr <- p.adjust(p_values, method = "BH")

# 4. Construct Top Differentially Methylated Positions (DMP) Table
dmp_table <- data.frame(
    Probe_ID = rownames(Beta_values),
    Mean_Beta_Cancer = mean_Beta_cancer,
    Mean_Beta_Normal = mean_Beta_normal,
    Delta_Beta = delta_Beta, # Positive = Hypermethylated in Cancer
    P_Value = p_values,
    FDR = fdr
)

# Sort by statistical significance
dmp_table <- dmp_table[order(dmp_table$P_Value), ]

# 5. Output Management
message("4. Exporting calculated matrices and statistical reports...")
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save the mathematical transformation matrices 
write.csv(Beta_values, file = file.path(output_dir, "beta_values_matrix.csv"), row.names = TRUE)
write.csv(M_values, file = file.path(output_dir, "m_values_matrix.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

# Save the differential methylation summary stats
write.csv(dmp_table, file = file.path(output_dir, "differential_methylation_stats.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Count Significant Probes (e.g., FDR < 0.05 and absolute DeltaBeta > 0.1)
sig_hyper <- sum(dmp_table$FDR < 0.05 & dmp_table$Delta_Beta > 0.1, na.rm = TRUE)
sig_hypo <- sum(dmp_table$FDR < 0.05 & dmp_table$Delta_Beta < -0.1, na.rm = TRUE)

message(sprintf("Analysis Complete! Found %d hypermethylated and %d hypomethylated CpGs.", sig_hyper, sig_hypo))

prompt: Read the gene-by-sample count matrix from `inputs/counts.tsv`, compute `log2(count + 1)`, and calculate the gene-gene Pearson correlation matrix. Define undirected associations by absolute correlation greater than 0.7, excluding self-links. For each gene, report its number of associations and its mean absolute correlation across the full correlation row as columns `gene`, `degree`, and `mean_correlation` in `outputs/ppi_stats.csv`.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# This script computes gene network statistics from expression correlations

# Read expression count data
expr <- read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', row.names = 1)

# Log2-transform the data with log2(count + 1) as specified
log_expr <- log2(expr + 1)

# Compute gene-gene Pearson correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(t(log_expr), method = 'pearson')

# Define network edges as gene pairs with absolute correlation above 0.7
threshold <- 0.7
adjacency <- abs(cor_matrix) > threshold
diag(adjacency) <- FALSE  # Remove self-loops

# Compute degree (number of connections per gene)
degree <- rowSums(adjacency)

# Compute mean absolute correlation for each gene
mean_abs_cor <- rowMeans(abs(cor_matrix) - diag(nrow(cor_matrix)))

write.csv(degree_df, 'outputs/ppi_stats.csv', row.names = FALSE)

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(phyloseq))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(vegan)) # Standard community ecology package used by phyloseq

# 1. Load Data
message("1. Loading OTU table, taxonomy, and sample data...")
otu_file <- file.path("inputs", "otu_table.csv")
tax_file <- file.path("inputs", "taxonomy.csv")
sample_file <- file.path("inputs", "sample_data.csv")

if (!file.exists(otu_file) || !file.exists(tax_file) || !file.exists(sample_file)) {
    stop("Input files not found.")
}

# Read CSVs into R objects
# OTU Table: Rows=Taxa, Cols=Samples
otu_mat <- read.csv(otu_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
otu_mat <- as.matrix(otu_mat)

# Taxonomy Table: Rows=Taxa, Cols=Ranks
tax_mat <- read.csv(tax_file, row.names = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
tax_mat <- as.matrix(tax_mat)

# Sample Data: Rows=Samples
sample_df <- read.csv(sample_file, row.names = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# 2. Construct Phyloseq Object
message("2. Creating phyloseq object...")
# We must ensure taxa are rows in otu_table
OTU <- otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
TAX <- tax_table(tax_mat)
SAM <- sample_data(sample_df)

ps <- phyloseq(OTU, TAX, SAM)

# 3. Pre-processing / Filtering
message("3. Pre-processing and filtering...")
# Basic filtering: Remove taxa with 0 counts in all samples (should be none based on save_data logic, but good practice)
ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps) > 0, ps)

# Rarefaction (Subsampling to even depth) is optional but common for alpha diversity
# Here we'll skip rarefaction to keep it simple and deterministic, assuming library sizes are reasonably comparable
# Or we can normalize by relative abundance for Beta diversity.

# 4. Alpha Diversity Analysis
message("4. Calculating Alpha Diversity (Shannon, Simpson)...")
# estimate_richness returns a data.frame with diversity indices
alpha_div <- estimate_richness(ps, measures = c("Shannon", "Simpson"))
# Add SampleID
alpha_div$SampleID <- rownames(alpha_div)
# Reorder
alpha_div <- alpha_div[, c("SampleID", setdiff(names(alpha_div), "SampleID"))]

# 5. Beta Diversity Analysis (Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity)
message("5. Calculating Beta Diversity (Bray-Curtis)...")
# Transform to relative abundance (percentages) for Bray-Curtis
# This is crucial because library sizes vary.
ps_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps, function(x) x / sum(x))
# Calculate distance matrix
dist_bc <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rel, method = "bray")

# Convert dist object to matrix for saving
dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist_bc)

# 6. Save outputs
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save Alpha Diversity Table
write.csv(alpha_div, file = file.path(output_dir, "alpha_diversity.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save Beta Diversity Matrix (Symmetric)
write.csv(dist_mat, file = file.path(output_dir, "bray_curtis_distance.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

# Save Processed Sample Metadata (with Alpha Diversity merged)
# Merging original metadata with alpha diversity is often useful
merged_meta <- merge(sample_df, alpha_div, by.x = "row.names", by.y = "SampleID")
# Rename Row.names back to SampleID
names(merged_meta)[names(merged_meta) == "Row.names"] <- "SampleID"
write.csv(merged_meta, file = file.path(output_dir, "sample_metadata_with_diversity.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save Phyloseq Object
saveRDS(ps, file = file.path(output_dir, "phyloseq_object.rds"))

message("Analysis complete. Results saved to outputs/")

prompt: Write R code to quantile-normalize a gene expression count matrix using preprocessCore. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(preprocessCore). The input expression matrix is in inputs/counts.tsv with genes as rows and samples as columns, and the aim is to make sample-wise distributions comparable so that downstream differential expression or clustering analyses are driven by biology rather than technical variability. Read this file into R as a numeric matrix, apply preprocessCore::normalize.quantiles while preserving the original row and column labels, and then calculate per-sample means and standard deviations before and after normalization as an intermediate summary, relying only on preprocessCore and standard R functions without bringing in any additional packages. Save the normalized matrix as a tab-separated file to outputs/quantile_normalized.tsv and write the before/after summary statistics as a CSV file to outputs/normalization_summary.csv, and as a basic quality control step, check that both files are created, review how the means and standard deviations change across samples, and ensure there are no unexpected NA values or obviously corrupted entries in the normalized matrix.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
library(preprocessCore)

counts <- as.matrix(read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
storage.mode(counts) <- "double"
normalized <- normalize.quantiles(counts)
dimnames(normalized) <- dimnames(counts)

if (!dir.exists('outputs')) dir.create('outputs', recursive = TRUE)
write.table(normalized, file = 'outputs/quantile_normalized.tsv', sep = '\t', quote = FALSE)

summary_df <- data.frame(
  sample = colnames(counts),
  mean_before = colMeans(counts),
  mean_after = colMeans(normalized),
  sd_before = apply(counts, 2, sd),
  sd_after = apply(normalized, 2, sd)
)
write.csv(summary_df, 'outputs/normalization_summary.csv', row.names = FALSE)
