prompt: Write R code to perform quantile normalization of a gene expression count matrix using preprocessCore. At the beginning, load the required packages: library(preprocessCore). The raw matrix is located at inputs/counts.tsv and represents gene-by-sample expression counts that need to be put on a common distribution so that downstream comparisons of expression levels and variance across samples are not confounded by technical differences. Use preprocessCore::normalize.quantiles.determine.target to derive an appropriate target distribution from the input counts, then apply preprocessCore::normalize.quantiles.use.target to the same matrix so that the normalized data preserve the original gene and sample structure; save the resulting normalized matrix as a tab-separated file at outputs/target_quantile.tsv and write the target distribution itself as a tab-separated file to outputs/target_distribution.tsv. After normalization, compute per-gene (row-wise) variance before and after normalization and summarize these in a CSV table with gene identifiers, writing this variance comparison to outputs/row_variance_changes.csv. Please rely only on preprocessCore and its documented functions for the normalization, and as a basic quality check confirm that all three output files are created, inspect simple variance summaries to ensure the distributions look reasonable, and verify that no unexpected NA values or extreme outliers were introduced.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
library(preprocessCore)

counts <- as.matrix(read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
storage.mode(counts) <- "double"
# Determine a target distribution using the input data
set.seed(42)
target <- normalize.quantiles.determine.target(counts, target.length = nrow(counts))
normalized <- normalize.quantiles.use.target(counts, target = target)
dimnames(normalized) <- dimnames(counts)

if (!dir.exists('outputs')) dir.create('outputs', recursive = TRUE)
write.table(normalized, file = 'outputs/target_quantile.tsv', sep = '\t', quote = FALSE)
write.table(target, file = 'outputs/target_distribution.tsv', sep = '\t', quote = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)

changes <- data.frame(
  gene = rownames(counts),
  variance_before = apply(counts, 1, var),
  variance_after = apply(normalized, 1, var)
)

prompt: Perform basic Quality Control (QC) on a FASTQ file using the 'ShortRead' package. Load the FASTQ from 'inputs/sample.fastq.gz'. Extract reads and quality scores. For each read, calculate its length, GC content (proportion of G + C), and average Phred quality score (mean ASCII value - 33). Save these per-read metrics (Read_ID, Length, GC_Content, Avg_Quality) to 'outputs/read_metrics.csv'. Calculate the overall base frequencies across all reads and save them to 'outputs/base_frequencies.csv'. Finally, compute overall summary statistics including 'Total_Reads', 'Total_Bases', 'Mean_Read_Length', 'Average_GC_Content', and 'Mean_Quality_Score', and save them to 'outputs/summary_statistics.csv'. Do not generate any plots.

### sample.fastq.gz (11,365 bytes)
[Binary file: 11,365 bytes; represented here by file metadata.]
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ShortRead))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Biostrings))

# 1. Load Data
message("1. Loading FASTQ file...")
fastq_file <- file.path("inputs", "sample.fastq.gz")
if (!file.exists(fastq_file)) stop("FASTQ file not found.")

# Read the entire FASTQ file into memory (assume it's a small subset)
# If large, FastqStreamer would be used instead.
fq <- readFastq(fastq_file)

# 2. Extract Read Information
message("2. Extracting read-level metrics...")

# Extract read sequences and quality scores
seqs <- sread(fq)
quals <- quality(fq)
ids <- as.character(id(fq))

# Calculate sequence lengths
read_lengths <- width(seqs)

# Calculate GC content per read
# letterFrequency returns a numeric matrix
gc_counts <- letterFrequency(seqs, letters = "GC", as.prob = FALSE)
read_gc_content <- rowSums(gc_counts) / read_lengths

# Calculate average quality score per read
# BStringSet can be coerced to integer matrix, representing ASCII codes
# Phred+33 encoding: the numerical quality is ASCII value - 33
qual_matrix <- as(quals, "matrix")
mean_quals <- rowMeans(qual_matrix, na.rm = TRUE) - 33

# Create read-level detail dataframe
read_df <- data.frame(
    Read_ID = sub(" .*", "", ids), # take only the first part of ID up to space
    Length = read_lengths,
    GC_Content = read_gc_content,
    Avg_Quality = mean_quals,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 3. Compute Summary Statistics for the Whole File
message("3. Computing summary statistics...")

# Total reads and total bases
total_reads <- length(fq)
total_bases <- sum(read_lengths)

# Overall nucleotide frequency (using alphabetFrequency)
# collapse = TRUE aggregates counts across all sequences in the DNAStringSet
nuc_freqs <- alphabetFrequency(seqs, collapse = TRUE, baseOnly = TRUE)

summary_df <- data.frame(
    Metric = c("Total_Reads", "Total_Bases", "Mean_Read_Length", "Average_GC_Content", "Mean_Quality_Score"),
    Value = c(
        total_reads,
        total_bases,
        mean(read_lengths),
        mean(read_gc_content),
        mean(mean_quals)
    )
)

# Table for base counts:
nuc_df <- data.frame(
    Base = names(nuc_freqs),
    Count = as.numeric(nuc_freqs)
)

# 4. Save Outputs
message("4. Saving output files...")
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save the read-level QC details
write.csv(read_df, file = file.path(output_dir, "read_metrics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save the file-level summary metrics
write.csv(summary_df, file = file.path(output_dir, "summary_statistics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save the base frequencies
write.csv(nuc_df, file = file.path(output_dir, "base_frequencies.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

message("Analysis complete. QC metrics saved to outputs/")

prompt: Perform Pathway Topology Analysis using the 'SPIA' package. Load the full differential expression table from 'inputs/diff_expr_results.csv' which contains columns 'EntrezID', 'Log2FoldChange', and 'FDR'. First, extract purely the background gene universe by taking all unique 'EntrezID's. Second, identify Significant Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) based on FDR < 0.05. Resolve duplicates by keeping the one with the maximum absolute 'Log2FoldChange' for each 'EntrezID'. Create a named numeric vector where values are 'Log2FoldChange' and names are 'EntrezID'. Run 'spia()' targeting the human organism ('hsa') with 2000 bootstraps (nB=2000), disabling all plots. Save the fully sorted (by 'pGFdr') SPIA results to 'outputs/spia_full_results.csv'. Extract pathways showing a significant global impact (pGFdr < 0.05) and save them to 'outputs/spia_significant_pathways.csv'. Save a final CSV 'outputs/spia_summary.csv' with columns 'Metric' and 'Value' documenting 'Total_Pathways_Analyzed', 'Significant_Pathways_Found', and 'Total_DEGs_Inputted'. Do not generate any graphical plots.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(SPIA))

# 1. Load Data
message("1. Loading differential expression results...")
input_file <- file.path("inputs", "diff_expr_results.csv")
if (!file.exists(input_file)) stop("Expression statistics file not found.")

diff_expr_df <- read.csv(input_file, colClasses = c("character", "character", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric"))

# 2. Extract Significant Genes and Universal Background
message("2. Filtering for Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs)...")
# SPIA requires:
# - A named numeric vector of the log2 fold changes for all SIGNIFICANT genes
# - A character vector containing all genes in the background universe

# Define significance criteria (FDR < 0.05)
is_sig <- diff_expr_df$FDR < 0.05
sig_genes_df <- diff_expr_df[is_sig, ]

# SPIA sometimes throws an error if there are duplicated Entrez IDs (e.g. multiple probes per gene).
# We take the one with the largest absolute logFC for each Entrez ID
sig_genes_df <- sig_genes_df[order(abs(sig_genes_df$Log2FoldChange), decreasing = TRUE), ]
sig_genes_df <- sig_genes_df[!duplicated(sig_genes_df$EntrezID), ]

# Format 1: Named Numeric Vector of Significant Log2 Fold Changes
sig_logfc <- sig_genes_df$Log2FoldChange
names(sig_logfc) <- sig_genes_df$EntrezID

# Format 2: Vector of ALL measured Entrez IDs (the gene universe)
# Need to remove duplicates here too
universe_genes <- unique(diff_expr_df$EntrezID)

message(sprintf("Found %d significant unique genes out of %d background genes.", length(sig_logfc), length(universe_genes)))

# 3. SPIA Pathway Topology Analysis
# SPIA uses both over-representation (PNDE) and perturbation (pPERT) metrics
# We use KEGG pathways by default for "hsa" (Homo sapiens)
message("3. Running SPIA (Signaling Pathway Impact Analysis)...")
# set seed for robust bootstrap p-values inside SPIA
set.seed(42)

# Run SPIA:
# de: named vector of logFC
# all: vector of ALL universe Entrez IDs
# organism: KEGG code ("hsa" for human)
# nB: Number of permutations for bootstrapping
# plots: FALSE as per task rules
spia_results <- spia(de = sig_logfc, all = universe_genes, organism = "hsa", nB = 2000, plots = FALSE, beta = NULL)

# 4. Process Results
message("4. Formatting and saving pathway results...")
# SPIA outputs columns like: Name, pSize, NDE, pNDE, tA, pPERT, pG, pGFdr, pGFWER
# Focus on the False Discovery Rate corrected global p-value (pGFdr)
# Sort by the most significant impacted pathways
spia_results_sorted <- spia_results[order(spia_results$pGFdr), ]

# Combine into outputs
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save the full SPIA impact table
write.csv(spia_results_sorted, file = file.path(output_dir, "spia_full_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Extract only the significantly impacted pathways (Global FDR < 0.05)
significant_pathways <- subset(spia_results_sorted, pGFdr < 0.05)
write.csv(significant_pathways, file = file.path(output_dir, "spia_significant_pathways.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Output summary metric table for task completion completeness
summary_stats <- data.frame(
    Metric = c("Total_Pathways_Analyzed", "Significant_Pathways_Found", "Total_DEGs_Inputted"),
    Value = c(nrow(spia_results), nrow(significant_pathways), length(sig_logfc))
)
write.csv(summary_stats, file = file.path(output_dir, "spia_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

message(sprintf("SPIA complete. Identified %d significantly impacted KEGG pathways.", nrow(significant_pathways)))
message("Results saved to outputs/")

prompt: Perform a standard survival analysis using the base R 'survival' package on the provided lung cancer dataset ('inputs/lung_clinical.csv'). First, clean the data by removing rows with missing 'ph.ecog' or 'sex' values. Convert 'sex' (1=Male, 2=Female) to a factor with appropriate labels. Calculate Kaplan-Meier survival estimates stratified by sex using 'survfit()' and extract the median survival times along with 95% confidence intervals; save this summary table to 'outputs/km_median_survival.csv'. Next, fit a Cox Proportional Hazards model ('coxph') to assess the effect of 'ph.ecog', 'sex', and 'age' on survival time ('time' and 'status'). Extract the Hazard Ratios, 95% confidence intervals, and p-values for each covariate into a clean table and save it as 'outputs/cox_model_results.csv'. Finally, save the fitted Cox model object as an RDS file to 'outputs/cox_model.rds'. Do not generate any plots.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))

# 1. Load input data
# Reads clinical data including time, status (censoring), and covariates
message("1. Loading clinical data...")
clinical_file <- file.path("inputs", "lung_clinical.csv")
if (!file.exists(clinical_file)) {
    stop("Input file 'inputs/lung_clinical.csv' not found.")
}
lung_data <- read.csv(clinical_file)

# 2. Data Cleaning
# Remove rows with NA in 'ph.ecog' (ECOG performance score) and 'sex' as we will model these
# The 'lung' dataset typically has missing values for some covariates
clean_data <- lung_data[!is.na(lung_data$ph.ecog) & !is.na(lung_data$sex), ]

# Recode sex: 1=Male, 2=Female in original dataset. Convert to factor for clarity.
# Using factor levels makes interpretation of coefficients safer.
clean_data$sex <- factor(clean_data$sex, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female"))

# 3. Create Survival Object
# The core object for survival analysis in R: Surv(time, status)
# status: 1=censored, 2=dead. The model usually expects 0/1 or TRUE/FALSE (dead).
# The survival function Surv() handles 1/2 coding automatically if specified?
# Actually, Surv() documentation says status: 'censoring status 1=censored, 2=dead'. 
# When type='right', 0/1, TRUE/FALSE, 1/2 are accepted. 2 implies event occurred.
surv_obj <- Surv(time = clean_data$time, event = clean_data$status)

# 4. Fit Cox Proportional Hazards Model
# Model: Survive ~ ECOG score + Sex + Age
# Assesses the effect of covariates on survival hazard
message("2. Fitting Cox Proportional Hazards model...")
cox_fit <- coxph(surv_obj ~ ph.ecog + sex + age, data = clean_data)

# 5. Extract Cox Model Results
# We want clean numerical output: Hazard Ratio (exp(coef)), 95% CI, P-value
cox_summary <- summary(cox_fit)
cox_table <- data.frame(
    term = rownames(cox_summary$coefficients),
    hazard_ratio = cox_summary$coefficients[, "exp(coef)"],
    lower_95 = cox_summary$conf.int[, "lower .95"],
    upper_95 = cox_summary$conf.int[, "upper .95"],
    p_value = cox_summary$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"],
    row.names = NULL
)

# 6. Fit Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves
# Univariate analysis: Survival by Sex
message("3. Calculating Kaplan-Meier estimates by Sex...")
km_fit <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ sex, data = clean_data)

# Extract median survival times
km_table <- summary(km_fit)$table
# Convert to clean dataframe
km_results <- data.frame(
    strata = rownames(km_table),
    records = km_table[, "records"],
    events = km_table[, "events"],
    median_survival = km_table[, "median"],
    lower_95 = km_table[, "0.95LCL"],
    upper_95 = km_table[, "0.95UCL"],
    row.names = NULL
)

# 7. Save outputs
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save Cox results
write.csv(cox_table, file = file.path(output_dir, "cox_model_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save KM median survival stats
write.csv(km_results, file = file.path(output_dir, "km_median_survival.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save the model object for potential future use (e.g. prediction)
saveRDS(cox_fit, file = file.path(output_dir, "cox_model.rds"))

message("Analysis complete. Results saved to outputs/")

prompt: Perform batch effect correction on microarray expression data using the 'sva' package. Load the expression matrix (rows=probes, cols=samples) from 'inputs/expression.csv' and the sample metadata from 'inputs/metadata.csv'. Create a model matrix using the 'Outcome' column as the biological covariate that must be preserved. Run the Empirical Bayes 'ComBat' function using the 'Batch' column to define the batches. Calculate the top 3 principal components (PC1, PC2, PC3) of the expression matrix using 'prcomp', both BEFORE correction and AFTER correction. Save the new batch-corrected expression matrix to 'outputs/combat_corrected_expression.csv'. Save the PCA coordinates joined with the metadata (SampleID, Batch, Outcome, PC1, PC2, PC3) to 'outputs/pca_uncorrected.csv' and 'outputs/pca_corrected.csv' respectively. Do not generate any plots.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(sva))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(stats))

# 1. Load Data
message("1. Loading expression data and phenotypes...")
expr_file <- file.path("inputs", "expression.csv")
meta_file <- file.path("inputs", "metadata.csv")

if (!file.exists(expr_file) || !file.exists(meta_file)) stop("Input files not found.")

# Read Expression matrix (Rows=Probes, Cols=Samples)
edata <- read.csv(expr_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
edata <- as.matrix(edata)

# Read Phenotype/Metadata (Rows=Samples)
pheno <- read.csv(meta_file, row.names = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# Ensure sample alignment
if (!identical(colnames(edata), rownames(pheno))) {
    stop("Sample names in expression matrix and metadata do not perfectly match.")
}

# 2. Extract Batch factor and build biological Model
message("2. Configuring biological covariates and batch assignments...")
batch <- pheno$Batch

# Build a model matrix describing the biological variables we want to PROTECT
# Here, we want to remove the batch effect but keep the variance associated with Cancer 'Outcome'
mod <- model.matrix(~as.factor(Outcome), data = pheno)

# 3. ComBat Correction
message("3. Running Empirical Bayes Batch Effect Correction (ComBat)...")
# ComBat uses parametric (par.prior=TRUE) or non-parametric priors
combat_edata <- ComBat(dat = edata, batch = batch, mod = mod, par.prior = TRUE, prior.plots = FALSE)

# 4. Numerically Evaluate the Correction (PCA Analysis)
message("4. Computing Principal Components before and after correction...")
# Run PCA on the original dataset 
# (prcomp requires samples as rows, so we transpose: t(edata))
pca_uncorrected <- prcomp(t(edata), scale. = TRUE)
pca_unc_df <- data.frame(
    SampleID = rownames(pheno),
    Batch = pheno$Batch,
    Outcome = pheno$Outcome,
    PC1 = pca_uncorrected$x[,1],
    PC2 = pca_uncorrected$x[,2],
    PC3 = pca_uncorrected$x[,3]
)

# Run PCA on the batch-corrected dataset
pca_corrected <- prcomp(t(combat_edata), scale. = TRUE)
pca_cor_df <- data.frame(
    SampleID = rownames(pheno),
    Batch = pheno$Batch,
    Outcome = pheno$Outcome,
    PC1 = pca_corrected$x[,1],
    PC2 = pca_corrected$x[,2],
    PC3 = pca_corrected$x[,3]
)

# 5. Save Outputs
message("5. Saving outputs...")
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save the transformed matrix (cleaned biological expression)
# Usually, downstream analysis (like limma) is performed on this matrix
write.csv(combat_edata, file = file.path(output_dir, "combat_corrected_expression.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

# Save PCA coordinates for empirical observation
# Without plotting, users can look at how PC1/PC2 correlates with Batch vs Outcome
write.csv(pca_unc_df, file = file.path(output_dir, "pca_uncorrected.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(pca_cor_df, file = file.path(output_dir, "pca_corrected.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

message("Analysis complete. ComBat expression & PCA metrics saved to outputs/")

prompt: Write R code to normalize RNA-seq count data to CPM (Counts Per Million) using base R. Read the raw count matrix from inputs/counts.tsv with genes as rows and samples as columns, compute each sample's library size, and then compute CPM for each gene as 1e6 * count / library_size. Save the resulting CPM-normalized expression matrix as outputs/cpm.csv, preserving gene row names. As a basic quality check, ensure the file is created and each sample's CPM column sums to roughly one million.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# CPM normalization adjusts for sequencing depth differences between samples

# Read raw count data from input file
counts <- read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', row.names = 1)

# Compute CPM normalization: (count / total_count_per_sample) * 1e6
# This normalizes each count by the library size (total counts per sample)
cpm <- sweep(counts, 2, colSums(counts), FUN = '/') * 1e6

# Save CPM normalized counts to output file
write.csv(cpm, 'outputs/cpm.csv', row.names = TRUE)

solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

prompt: Normalize the raw gene-by-sample count matrix in inputs/counts.tsv to counts per million using base R. Treat the first column as gene identifiers, calculate each sample's library size, divide counts by library_size / 1e6, and write the normalized matrix to outputs/cpm.tsv as a tab-separated file with gene row names and no quotes.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# CPM (Counts Per Million) normalization for RNA-seq count data
# Adjusts for library size differences between samples

# Read raw counts from input file
counts <- read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

# Calculate library sizes (total counts per sample)
lib_sizes <- colSums(counts)

# Normalize to CPM: divide each count by (library_size / 1e6)
# This gives counts per million reads
cpm <- sweep(counts, 2, lib_sizes / 1e6, FUN = "/")

# Save CPM normalized data
write.table(cpm, 'outputs/cpm.tsv', sep = "\t", row.names = TRUE, quote = FALSE)

prompt: Write R code to normalize RNA-seq count data to TPM (Transcripts Per Million) using base R. Do not assume the existence of a tcga package. Instead, implement TPM normalization directly using base R operations. Read the gene × sample count matrix from inputs/counts.tsv and gene lengths from inputs/gene_lengths.tsv (lengths should be in base pairs or kilobases; specify the unit in your code or assume kilobases). For each gene, compute RPK (Reads Per Kilobase) as count / length_kb. For each sample, compute the sum of RPK values across all genes, then compute TPM as 1e6 * RPK / sum(RPK). Save the TPM-normalized expression matrix to outputs/tpm.tsv, preserving gene row names and sample column names. As a basic quality check, confirm that the file is created, each sample's TPM column sums to roughly one million, and the values are non-negative and reasonable.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# TPM (Transcripts Per Million) normalization for RNA-seq data
# Normalizes for both gene length and sequencing depth

# Read raw counts and gene lengths from input files
counts <- read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
# Note: gene lengths file expected
gene_lengths <- read.table('inputs/gene_lengths.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', row.names = 1)

# Step 1: Calculate RPK (reads per kilobase) - normalize by gene length
rpk <- sweep(counts, 1, gene_lengths[rownames(counts), 1] / 1000, FUN = "/")

# Step 2: Calculate TPM - normalize by sequencing depth
# Divide by sum of RPK per sample and multiply by 1 million
tpm <- sweep(rpk, 2, colSums(rpk) / 1e6, FUN = "/")

# Save TPM normalized data
write.table(tpm, 'outputs/tpm.tsv', sep = "\t", row.names = TRUE, quote = FALSE)

prompt: Using edgeR, read counts from `inputs/expression.tsv` and metadata from `inputs/clinical.tsv`, align metadata to count columns by `sample`, and treat `group` as a factor. Build a DGEList, calculate normalization factors, use a `~ group` design, estimate dispersion, fit a GLM, and run the likelihood-ratio test. Save all rows from `topTags(..., n = Inf)$table`, including gene row names, to `outputs/deg_results.csv`.
solution_r:
library(edgeR)

# Read counts and clinical data
counts <- read.table('inputs/expression.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
clinical <- read.table('inputs/clinical.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
clinical <- clinical[match(colnames(counts), clinical$sample), , drop = FALSE]
clinical$group <- factor(clinical$group)

# Create DGEList and design matrix
dge <- DGEList(counts = counts)
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)
design <- model.matrix(~ group, data = clinical)

# Estimate dispersion and fit model
dge <- estimateDisp(dge, design)
fit <- glmFit(dge, design)
lrt <- glmLRT(fit)

# Extract results
results <- topTags(lrt, n = Inf)$table
write.csv(results, 'outputs/deg_results.csv', row.names = TRUE)

solution_r:
library(DESeq2)

# Read counts and clinical data
counts <- read.table('inputs/expression.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
clinical <- read.table('inputs/clinical.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

results <- results(dds)

prompt: Using edgeR and limma, read counts from `inputs/counts.tsv` and metadata from `inputs/clinical.tsv`. Create a DGEList, calculate normalization factors, build a `~ group` design from the clinical rows in their supplied order, run `voom` without plotting, fit the linear model, and apply empirical Bayes moderation. Save all rows from `topTable` for coefficient 2, including gene row names, to `outputs/limma_voom_results.csv`.
solution_r:
library(limma)
library(edgeR)

# Read counts and clinical data
counts <- read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
clinical <- read.table('inputs/clinical.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

design <- model.matrix(~ group, data = clinical)

v <- voom(dge, design, plot = FALSE)

fit <- eBayes(fit)

results <- topTable(fit, coef = 2, n = Inf)
write.csv(results, 'outputs/limma_voom_results.csv', row.names = TRUE)

prompt: Write R code to perform Gene Ontology Biological Process enrichment for the gene symbols in the first column of inputs/counts.tsv. solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(clusterProfiler)
  library(org.Hs.eg.db)
})

counts_path <- file.path("inputs", "counts.tsv")
if (!file.exists(counts_path)) stop("counts.tsv missing")

counts <- read.delim(
  counts_path,
  row.names = 1,
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
genes <- unique(rownames(counts))
genes <- genes[!is.na(genes) & nzchar(genes)]
if (!length(genes)) stop("counts.tsv contains no gene symbols")

go_enrich <- enrichGO(
  gene = genes,
  OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db,
  keyType = "SYMBOL",
  ont = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  qvalueCutoff = 0.2,
  readable = FALSE
)
results <- as.data.frame(go_enrich)

dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.table(
  results,
  file.path("outputs", "go_enrichment.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE,
  na = ""
)

prompt: Set the R seed to 1000 and read `inputs/counts.tsv` with gene IDs as row names. For any zero-variance gene, add independent normal noise with standard deviation `1e-6`, then run scaled PCA on the transposed matrix. Write sample coordinates for PC1 through PC5 plus `sample` to `outputs/pca_coordinates.tsv`, and write columns `PC` and `variance` for the first five variance proportions to `outputs/variance_explained.csv`.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on expression data
# Reduces dimensionality and identifies major sources of variation

# Read expression data from input file
set.seed(1000)
expr <- read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

expr_mat <- as.matrix(expr)
zero_sd <- apply(expr_mat, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE) == 0
if (any(zero_sd)) {
  noise <- matrix(rnorm(sum(zero_sd) * ncol(expr_mat), sd = 1e-6), nrow = sum(zero_sd))
  expr_mat[zero_sd, ] <- expr_mat[zero_sd, , drop = FALSE] + noise
}

pca_result <- prcomp(t(expr_mat), scale. = TRUE)

# Extract and save PCA coordinates for first 5 principal components
pca_coords <- as.data.frame(pca_result$x[, 1:5])
pca_coords$sample <- rownames(pca_coords)
write.table(pca_coords, 'outputs/pca_coordinates.tsv', sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

# Calculate and save variance explained by each PC
variance_explained <- summary(pca_result)$importance[2, 1:5]
write.csv(data.frame(PC = paste0('PC', 1:5), variance = variance_explained),
          'outputs/variance_explained.csv', row.names = FALSE)

solution_r:
library(SummarizedExperiment)

run_task <- function(work_dir) {
  counts_file <- file.path(work_dir, "inputs", "counts.tsv")
  clinical_file <- file.path(work_dir, "inputs", "clinical.tsv")
  
  counts <- read.table(counts_file, sep="\t", header=TRUE, row.names=1)
  clinical <- read.table(clinical_file, sep="\t", header=TRUE)
  
  # Ensure order
  common <- intersect(colnames(counts), clinical$barcode)
  counts <- counts[, common]
  clinical <- clinical[match(common, clinical$barcode), ]
  
  se <- SummarizedExperiment(assays=list(counts=as.matrix(counts)),
                             colData=DataFrame(clinical))
                             
  # Save output for evaluation
  write.csv(assay(se), file.path(work_dir, "outputs", "se_counts.csv"))
  
  return(se)
}

run_task(getwd())

prompt: Load 'clinical.tsv' from the 'inputs' directory. Create a 'status' column (1 if 'vital_status' is 'Dead', 0 otherwise). Create a 'time' column: use 'days_to_death' if 'status' is 1, otherwise use 'days_to_last_follow_up'. Filter out samples where 'time' or 'gender' is NA. Fit a Kaplan-Meier survival curve (`survfit`) using `Surv(time, status)` stratified by 'gender'. Extract the survival summary table (time, n.risk, n.event, n.censor, surv) and save it to 'outputs/survival_summary.csv'. Return the `survfit` object.
solution_r:
library(survival)

run_task <- function(work_dir) {
  clinical_file <- file.path(work_dir, "inputs", "clinical.tsv")
  clinical <- read.table(clinical_file, sep="\t", header=TRUE)
  
  # Preprocess status
  clinical$status <- ifelse(clinical$vital_status == "Dead", 1, 0)
  
  # Preprocess time
  clinical$time <- ifelse(clinical$status == 1, clinical$days_to_death, clinical$days_to_last_follow_up)
  
  # Filter
  clinical <- clinical[!is.na(clinical$time) & !is.na(clinical$gender), ]
  
  fit <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ gender, data = clinical)
  
  # Save summary
  summ <- summary(fit)
  res_df <- data.frame(
    time = summ$time,
    n.risk = summ$n.risk,
    n.event = summ$n.event,
    n.censor = summ$n.censor,
    surv = summ$surv,
    strata = summ$strata
  )
  write.csv(res_df, file.path(work_dir, "outputs", "survival_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  
  return(fit)
}

run_task(getwd())

prompt: Write R code to perform per-protein t tests between two groups. Read inputs/counts.tsv and inputs/clinical.tsv, define group1 and group2 using unique(clinical$group)[1] and unique(clinical$group)[2], run t.test for each protein, compute fc = mean(group2) / mean(group1), and write a CSV with columns protein, pvalue, fc to outputs/t_test_results.csv using write.csv with row.names=FALSE.
solution_r:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Perform t-tests on protein expression between two groups
# Identifies differentially abundant proteins

# Read protein expression and clinical data from input files
protein_expr <- read.table('inputs/counts.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
clinical <- read.table('inputs/clinical.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Identify samples for each group
group1_samples <- clinical$sample[clinical$group == unique(clinical$group)[1]]
group2_samples <- clinical$sample[clinical$group == unique(clinical$group)[2]]

# Perform t-test for each protein comparing two groups
t_test_results <- apply(protein_expr, 1, function(protein) {
  t.test(protein[group1_samples], protein[group2_samples])
})

# Extract p-values and fold changes from t-test results
results_df <- data.frame(
  protein = rownames(protein_expr),
  pvalue = sapply(t_test_results, function(x) x$p.value),
  fc = rowMeans(protein_expr[, group2_samples]) / rowMeans(protein_expr[, group1_samples])
)

# Save t-test results
write.csv(results_df, 'outputs/t_test_results.csv', row.names = FALSE)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Perform ANOVA on protein expression across multiple groups
# Tests for differential abundance across more than two groups

  df <- data.frame(expression = protein, group = clinical$group)

  pvalue = anova_results
)

  expr_file <- file.path(work_dir, "inputs", "protein_expression.tsv")

  expr <- expr[rowSums(is.na(expr)) == 0, ]

solution_r:
run_task <- function(work_dir) {
  expr_file <- file.path(work_dir, "inputs", "protein_expression.tsv")
  expr <- read.table(expr_file, sep="\t", header=TRUE, row.names=1)
  
  expr <- expr[rowSums(is.na(expr)) == 0, ]
  
  vars <- apply(expr, 1, var)
  
  # Handle case with fewer than 10
  n_top <- min(10, length(vars))
  
  top_genes <- names(sort(vars, decreasing = TRUE))[1:n_top]

  return(subset_expr)
}

prompt: Perform transcriptome isoform-level data aggregation using the 'tximport' package. You are given pseudo-aligned Salmon output directories mapped within 'inputs/salmon' across multiple patients. The specific SampleIDs and their condition groups reside in 'inputs/metadata.csv'. A reference lookup mapping Ensembl transcript IDs to Ensembl Gene IDs is given in 'inputs/tx2gene.csv'. Construct vectors linking directly to the 'quant.sf.gz' files in the respective sample folders using the metadata correctly. Run 'tximport()' defining 'type = "salmon"' and 'ignoreTxVersion = TRUE' while scaling the counts accurately assigning 'countsFromAbundance = "lengthScaledTPM"'. After pulling metrics, filter out background noise by explicitly selecting genes where row sums stringently evaluate uniquely to > 10 across all combined counts metrics in the full counts matrix. Apply this specific filtered indices list dynamically to both the count matrix and the inferred TPM abundance matrix. Map the completed final gene counts to 'outputs/aggregated_gene_counts.csv'  along with their matched corresponding raw TPM metrics to 'outputs/aggregated_gene_tpm.csv'. Establish a numerical overview outlining the process dimensions named 'outputs/tximport_summary.csv'. No visual density graphs plotted.
solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tximport))

# 1. Configuration and mapping 
message("1. Scanning local system for pseudo-aligned transcriptomics files (Salmon)...")
meta_file <- file.path("inputs", "metadata.csv")
tx2gene_file <- file.path("inputs", "tx2gene.csv")
salmon_dir <- file.path("inputs", "salmon")

if (!file.exists(meta_file) || !file.exists(tx2gene_file)) {
    stop("Required experimental metadata or tx2gene indices missing.")
}

# 2. Loading Meta Information
metadata <- read.csv(meta_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
tx2gene <- read.csv(tx2gene_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Build file paths strictly mapping to experimental grouping identifiers
# We map SampleID directly to their explicit quant.sf.gz file locations 
files <- file.path(salmon_dir, metadata$SampleID, "quant.sf.gz")
names(files) <- metadata$SampleID

if (any(!file.exists(files))) {
    stop("One or more target 'quant.sf.gz' files could not be located inside inputs/salmon/")
}

# 3. Running TXIMPORT execution
message("2. Executing tximport over transcript indices scaling towards gene-level metrics...")
message("This parses Ensembl IDs and aggregates transcript fragments mathematically.")

# A special quirk with Salmon: Tx IDs outputted often carry version numbers like '.1', '.2'
# But classical Ensembl references don't.
# The 'ignoreTxVersion = TRUE' elegantly patches disjointed matches between FASTA and GTF conventions
txi <- tximport(files, 
                type = "salmon", 
                tx2gene = tx2gene, 
                ignoreTxVersion = TRUE, 
                countsFromAbundance = "lengthScaledTPM")

# 4. Filter empty noise
message("3. Filtering biologically unexpressed fragments...")
# Extract aggregated counts matrix
# Use raw counts scaled by length as recommended for downstream DESeq2 analysis
count_matrix <- txi$counts
# Keep only genes having at least 1 count across ALL samples combined
count_matrix <- count_matrix[rowSums(count_matrix) > 10, ]

# Also extract the true TPMs (Transcripts per Million) used for absolute comparative expressions
tpm_matrix <- txi$abundance
# subset to same genes
tpm_matrix <- tpm_matrix[rownames(count_matrix), ]

# 5. Output management simulating downstream integration readiness
message("4. Exporting calculated read abundances into structured matrices...")
output_dir <- "outputs"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# Save Aggregated Raw Equivalent Counts
write.csv(count_matrix, file = file.path(output_dir, "aggregated_gene_counts.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

# Save Biological Scale Mapping (TPM)
write.csv(tpm_matrix, file = file.path(output_dir, "aggregated_gene_tpm.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

# Compile a quick evaluation metric
summary_stats <- data.frame(
    Metric = c("Total_Samples", "Total_Aggregated_Genes", "Median_Counts_Per_Gene"),
    Value = c(ncol(count_matrix), nrow(count_matrix), median(count_matrix))
)
write.csv(summary_stats, file = file.path(output_dir, "tximport_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

message(sprintf("Conversion complete! Successfully shrunk %d transcripts into %d biologically functional scaled genes.", nrow(txi$counts), nrow(count_matrix)))

solution_r:
dataset <- read.delim(file.path("inputs", "dataset.tsv"), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
visits <- read.delim(file.path("inputs", "visits.tsv"), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
visits <- visits[order(visits$USUBJID, visits$PARAMCD, visits$AVISITN), , drop = FALSE]
dataset <- dataset[order(dataset$USUBJID, dataset$PARAMCD, dataset$AVISITN), , drop = FALSE]
result_df <- visits
result_df$AVAL <- NA_real_
result_df$DTYPE <- ""
for (i in seq_len(nrow(result_df))) {
  prior <- dataset[
    dataset$USUBJID == result_df$USUBJID[i] &
      dataset$PARAMCD == result_df$PARAMCD[i] &
      dataset$AVISITN <= result_df$AVISITN[i],
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  if (nrow(prior) > 0) {
    prior <- prior[order(prior$AVISITN), , drop = FALSE]

}

solution_r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(admiral))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(rlang))

read_scalar <- function(path, column, default = "") {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(default)
  data <- read.delim(path, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (!nrow(data)) return(default)
  if (column %in% names(data)) return(as.character(data[[column]][1]))
  as.character(data[[1]][1])
}

read_key_values <- function(path) {
  data <- read.delim(path, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  values <- as.list(as.character(data$value))
  names(values) <- as.character(data$variable)
  values
}

parse_expr_list <- function(text) {
  parts <- trimws(strsplit(text, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
  parts <- parts[nzchar(parts)]
  rlang::parse_exprs(parts)
}

expr_label <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) return("")
  rlang::as_label(x)
}

exprs_label <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) return("")
  labels <- vapply(x, rlang::as_label, character(1))
  names_x <- names(x)
  if (is.null(names_x)) names_x <- rep("", length(labels))
  labels <- ifelse(nzchar(names_x), paste0(names_x, "=", labels), labels)
  paste(labels, collapse = ";")
}

dataset_name <- read_scalar(file.path("inputs", "dataset_name.tsv"), "dataset_name")
condition_text <- read_scalar(file.path("inputs", "condition.tsv"), "condition")
order <- parse_expr_list(read_scalar(file.path("inputs", "order.tsv"), "order"))
join_vars <- parse_expr_list(read_scalar(file.path("inputs", "join_vars.tsv"), "join_vars"))
join_type <- read_scalar(file.path("inputs", "join_type.tsv"), "join_type")
set_values <- read_key_values(file.path("inputs", "set_values_to.tsv"))
description <- read_scalar(file.path("inputs", "description.tsv"), "description")

event_def <- admiral::event_joined(
  dataset_name = dataset_name,
  condition = !!rlang::parse_expr(condition_text),
  order = order,
  join_vars = join_vars,
  join_type = join_type,
  set_values_to = rlang::exprs(!!!set_values),
  description = description
)

result <- data.frame(
  class = paste(class(event_def), collapse = "|"),
  description = event_def$description,
  dataset_name = event_def$dataset_name,
  condition = expr_label(event_def$condition),
  order = exprs_label(event_def$order),
  join_vars = exprs_label(event_def$join_vars),
  join_type = event_def$join_type,
  first_cond_lower = expr_label(event_def$first_cond_lower),
  first_cond_upper = expr_label(event_def$first_cond_upper),
  set_values_to = exprs_label(event_def$set_values_to),
  keep_source_vars = exprs_label(event_def$keep_source_vars),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(result, file.path("outputs", "result.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggsurvfit))

parse_scale_list <- function(fname) {
  df <- read.delim(file.path("inputs", fname), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  txt <- trimws(as.character(df[[1]][1]))
  value <- eval(parse(text = txt))
  if (!is.list(value)) {
    stop(fname, " must contain an expression that evaluates to a list")
  }
  value
}

x_scales <- parse_scale_list("x_scales.tsv")
y_scales <- parse_scale_list("y_scales.tsv")
result <- ggsurvfit::scale_ggsurvfit(x_scales = x_scales, y_scales = y_scales)

  scale_classes = paste(class(result), collapse = "|"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

solution_r:
df <- read.delim(file.path("inputs", "df.tsv"), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
df$nested_level <- as.integer(df$nested_level)
df$group_level <- as.integer(df$group_level)

df$indent <- ifelse(
  grepl("BY_HEADER", df$row_type) | df$row_type == "HEADER",
  df$group_level + table_offset,
  ifelse(
    df$row_type == "N",
    1L + df$group_level + table_offset,
    ifelse(
      df$row_type == "VALUE",
      2L + df$group_level + table_offset,
      ifelse(df$row_type == "NESTED", df$nested_level + df$group_level + table_offset, 0L)
    )
  )
)

write.csv(df, file.path("outputs", "result.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
